description:
Programme or Project Overview

Lund University invites applications for a doctoral student position in Technology and Society within the MSCA REGULAIRE doctoral network. The project studies regulatory learning and supervisory competence in the implementation of the EU AI Act, examining how supervisory authorities build the knowledge, routines and organisational capacity needed to govern artificial intelligence. The doctoral candidate will investigate how regulators learn across cases and sectors, and how supervisory competence develops in practice as AI oversight becomes a legal obligation across Europe.

REGULAIRE is a Marie Sklodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) doctoral network bringing together universities, regulators and civil-society partners across several European countries. The doctoral position at Lund is a salaried appointment under the Swedish collective agreement, and network membership adds structured training schools, secondments with partner organisations and regular joint supervision. The position suits a candidate who wants to work at the intersection of law, technology and public administration with a European research community.

Candidate profile and network training

Applicants hold a master's degree in law, science and technology studies, public administration, artificial intelligence or a related field, and can combine doctrinal or empirical analysis with an interest in how regulation actually works. Strong written English is required, and experience with qualitative or comparative methods is an advantage. Applications run through Lund University's Varbi portal with a CV, transcripts, references and a motivation letter, following the MSCA mobility rules that apply to doctoral candidates in the network.

Highlights

  • Doctoral position in the MSCA REGULAIRE doctoral network
  • Regulatory learning under the EU AI Act
  • Research on supervisory authorities and AI governance
  • Salaried employment per the Swedish collective agreement
  • Network training schools and secondments across Europe
  • Interdisciplinary environment at Lund University

Programme or Project Overview

The University of Essex recruits a Doctoral Research Fellow in the Department of Government within the DIViNE MSCA Doctoral Network on political violence and democracy. The fellow will pursue doctoral research on political violence, institutional reform and democratic resilience, contributing to the network's comparative research programme. Essex's Department of Government is one of the UK's leading political science departments, with long-standing research strengths in conflict, democracy and political behaviour.

The appointment carries a salary of GBP 38,784 - GBP 46,049 per annum, reflecting the MSCA doctoral candidate conditions, and includes network-level training, secondments and joint supervision across DIViNE partner institutions. The vacancy page lists a closing date of 11 November 2026, while the DIViNE network's application deadline is 15 November 2026, so candidates should prepare their materials early. The fellow will be based in Colchester with access to Essex's research centres and data resources.

Candidate profile and application route

Applicants hold a strong master's degree in political science, government or a related social-science field, with demonstrated interest in political violence or democracy research and suitable quantitative or mixed-methods skills. MSCA mobility rules apply to doctoral candidates in the network, so applicants must not have resided or carried out their main activity in the UK for more than 12 of the last 36 months. Applications are submitted through the University of Essex online recruitment system with a CV, transcripts, references and a research statement.

Programme or Project Overview

UMC Utrecht recruits a promotendus (doctoral candidate) for a 48-month project on the inclusion of children with disabilities (inclusie van kinderen met beperkingen), starting in January 2027. Many children with disabilities still face barriers in school, care and everyday social life, and inclusive approaches require evidence on what works in practice. The doctoral project studies inclusion from the perspectives of children, families and professionals, using participatory research approaches that give children a genuine voice in the research.

The position is for 32 hours per week with a salary of EUR 3,217 - EUR 4,077 gross per month under the Dutch CAO-NU collective agreement, based at UMC Utrecht, including the Wilhelmina Children's Hospital research environment. The doctoral candidate will conduct qualitative and participatory studies, collaborate with schools and care organisations, and contribute to implementation of findings in paediatric care and education. Because the research involves Dutch-speaking children, families and professionals, Dutch proficiency is required.

Candidate profile and working environment

Applicants hold a master's degree in health sciences, education, pedagogy or a related field, with an interest in child participation and disability research. Experience with qualitative or participatory methods and working with children is an advantage. UMC Utrecht offers structured doctoral training and a multidisciplinary environment spanning paediatrics, rehabilitation and social sciences.

  • Inclusion of children with disabilities

Maynooth University invites applications for a 36-month postdoctoral researcher position on the BIOCHAR project, focused on life cycle assessment of biochar systems. The researcher will quantify the environmental and climate performance of biochar production and application pathways, from feedstock sourcing and pyrolysis to field application, using established LCA methods and Irish and European datasets. Applicants hold a PhD in environmental science, environmental engineering, chemistry, process engineering or a closely related discipline, with demonstrable experience in life cycle assessment or comparable environmental systems analysis. Liverpool John Moores University recruits a post-doctoral research fellow in peat paludiculture biogeochemistry and ecology for a two-year fixed-term position. Programme or Project Overview

The Global Korea Scholarship (GKS) for graduate degrees is the Korean government's flagship scholarship for international master's and PhD students, administered by the National Institute for International Education (NIIED) under the Ministry of Education. Each year more than a thousand candidates are selected worldwide through two application tracks: the embassy track, which runs through Korean embassies in each country, and the university track, which runs directly through designated Korean universities.

The award covers full tuition at Korean universities, a monthly allowance, round-trip airfare, medical insurance, a settlement and language-training allowance and degree-completion grants. All scholars begin with a one-year intensive Korean language programme before starting their master's or PhD, which makes the scholarship suitable for applicants without prior Korean language skills. Applications for the 2027 graduate round open with the publication of the official GKS-G notice, and embassy-track deadlines typically fall between February and March 2027 depending on the country.

Application tracks and timeline

In the embassy track, candidates submit their dossier to the Korean embassy in their country of citizenship, which pre-screens and forwards recommended candidates to NIIED and the second-round universities. In the university track, candidates apply directly to up to three designated universities, which recommend successful applicants to NIIED. Both tracks conclude with NIIED's final evaluation, and scholars arrive in Korea in late summer 2027 for the language year. Applicants should prepare transcripts, diplomas, two recommendation letters, a personal statement, a study plan and proof of citizenship well before the notice is published.

Programme or Project Overview

The NL Scholarship is the Dutch national grant for international students from outside the European Economic Area who come to the Netherlands for a full-time bachelor's or master's programme. The scheme, formerly known as the Holland Scholarship, is financed by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science together with Dutch research universities and universities of applied sciences. It is now administered and promoted through the Study in NL platform.

The scholarship awards EUR 5,000 in the first year of study at participating institutions. Many universities combine the NL Scholarship with their own additional grants, so the total package can be larger at some institutions. Applications are made through the chosen Dutch university, and each institution sets its own selection criteria, so candidates should check the specific requirements and deadlines of their target programme alongside the national round.

Who should apply

The grant is aimed at non-EEA students applying for a full-time qualifying bachelor's or master's programme at a participating Dutch institution, who do not yet hold a degree from Dutch higher education. Selection is typically based on academic merit, motivation and the fit between the applicant's background and the chosen programme. Because the award is a one-off contribution towards study costs rather than a full scholarship, most successful applicants combine it with university-specific scholarships, part-time work rules available to student-visa holders, or other national schemes listed on the Study in NL scholarship finder.

  • EUR 5,000 grant in the first year of study
  • Open for bachelor's and master's programmes at participating universities

description:
Programme or Project Overview

Aarhus University invites applications for a PhD position on tracking microbes across borders using genomics to uncover biomass-to-biogas transmission pathways. The project applies genomic and bioinformatic methods to understand how microbial communities move through biomass supply chains and biogas plants, connecting findings to process performance in the bioenergy sector. The position is embedded in the university's research on green transition technologies and circular bioeconomy systems.

The successful candidate will combine field sampling, sequencing data generation and computational analysis to trace microbial populations across national borders and industrial sites. The work connects molecular microbiology with engineering practice, and findings will feed into improved inoculation, monitoring and risk-management strategies for biogas production. The PhD is a salaried three-year position under the Danish collective agreement, based at the Aarhus campus with project-related travel.

Project approach

The project builds on genome-resolved metagenomics and comparative genomics to identify microbial strains, follow their transmission routes and relate them to biogas process outcomes. The candidate will develop analysis pipelines, work with industrial and research partners, and publish findings in international journals. Applicants should hold a master's degree in microbiology, bioinformatics, environmental engineering or a related discipline, and demonstrate skills in genomics data analysis; experience with anaerobic digestion or bioprocess engineering is an advantage.

Highlights

  • Genome-resolved metagenomics of microbial communities
  • Transmission pathway analysis across borders and sites
  • Biomass-to-biogas process microbiology
  • Bioinformatics pipeline development
  • Collaboration with bioenergy industry partners
  • Salaried three-year PhD under the Danish collective agreement

The doctoral training runs through the UMCG's graduate programme with a supervisory team spanning health services research and organisational sociology.

Programme or Project Overview

Leiden University invites applications for a post-doctoral researcher working on agent-based modelling of Pleistocene landscape connectivity in Europe. The project simulates how Pleistocene environments connected and disconnected habitats and populations across the continent, informing debate in palaeoanthropology, archaeology and palaeoclimate research.

The postdoc will design and implement agent-based models that couple reconstructions of Pleistocene climate, vegetation and topography with movement and subsistence behaviour, and will run systematic simulation experiments across glacial and interglacial conditions. Results feed into European research collaborations on human-environment dynamics in deep time.

Project Overview

The University of Basel's Swiss Nanoscience Institute invites applications for a PhD position within the PhD programme in Nanoscience. The research aims to engineer environmentally (cell)-instructive hydrogels with controlled architecture (pore size, network interconnectivity) and mechanical properties (viscoelasticity) to recapitulate the mechanical micro-environment of the jawbone.

Mechanosensitive complexes within the hydrogel form stimuli-responsive cross-links that adjust hydrogel viscoelasticity as a function of cytoskeletal tension, guiding cell growth. You will combine biomaterials engineering, cell experiments, and computational modelling.

About FIBE3

FIBE3 stands for Future Infrastructure and Built Environment: Unlocking Net Zero. It is an EPSRC Centre for Doctoral Training based at the University of Cambridge. The programme aims to train researchers capable of addressing infrastructure challenges associated with the transition towards net zero. The programme combines a one-year Master of Research with a three-year PhD.

Four Main Research Themes

FIBE3 research is organised around four broad themes: current and disruptive technologies; circularity and whole-life approaches; AI-driven digitalisation and data; and risk-based systems thinking and connectivity. Students work closely with academic researchers and industrial partners.

Programme Structure

Year 1 – MRes: During the first year, students develop interdisciplinary knowledge of infrastructure; net-zero research skills; technical training; research methods; professional skills; and a detailed PhD research plan. Years 2–4 – PhD: The following three years focus on the student's doctoral research project. Projects involve academic supervision and industry collaboration and are expected to align with the FIBE3 research roadmap.

Funding

The University states that EPSRC FIBE3 studentships provide tuition-fee funding and maintenance support for eligible Home students. International applicants can apply, but the situation is significantly more competitive. The CDT states that a very small number of outstanding international applicants may receive support at a later stage in recruitment. Where such funding is awarded, the CDT may cover Home-rate tuition fees, stipend, and potentially an international-fee shortfall through additional University support. International funding should therefore not be considered guaranteed.

Academic Requirements

Applicants are generally expected to have a high UK 2:1 or First-Class degree, or an equivalent international qualification. Relevant academic backgrounds can include: civil engineering; mechanical engineering; chemical engineering; manufacturing engineering; electrical engineering; information engineering; materials science; environmental science; earth science; computer science; mathematics; chemistry; architecture; project management; and other related disciplines. Applicants must normally have completed at least a three-year undergraduate degree.

Application Routes

General Application: Applicants can propose their own research direction and explain how it aligns with FIBE3 themes. They should identify relevant academic supervisors and potential industry partners. Project-Specific Application: Applicants can apply for one of the advertised FIBE3 projects where a supervisor and industry partner are already identified. A research proposal is still expected even for project-specific applications.

Deadline

The current Cambridge FIBE3 page states: 14 April 2027. Applications may close sooner if all places are filled.

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the deadline: 14 April 2027 (or earlier if all places are filled). Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.

Wolfson Postgraduate Scholarships in the Humanities

With generous funding from The Wolfson Foundation, we are now inviting applications for Wolfson Postgraduate Scholarships starting in the 2027/28 academic year for doctoral (PhD) study in the broad subject areas of history, literature and languages.

The Wolfson Foundation awards funding to outstanding students who demonstrate potential to make an impact on their chosen field. Wolfson Scholarships will be awarded solely on academic merit. Ideally, the successful applicants should aspire to becoming significant contributors to society, whether in the academic sphere or in other areas of intellectual and cultural leadership.

Application deadline: 19 January 2027, midday.

Eligibility criteria

The awards are open to UK and International (including EU) applicants who will commence campus-based doctoral (PhD) study at the University of Nottingham at the start of the relevant academic year.

  • Applicants' intended PhD research must be in the discipline(s) of history, literature or languages (these are broadly drawn, please see Definition of eligible subject disciplines below)
  • Applicants should be resident in the UK for the duration of their studies and live within reasonable distance of UoN (except for periods of fieldwork)
  • Applicants should have a track record of academic excellence. This will usually be demonstrated by:
  • a good undergraduate degree, usually a first-class honours degree resulting in a BA
  • AND EITHER a Master's degree in a field of study relevant to their proposed doctoral research (the Master's must either be held at the point of application or completed by the time an applicant begins their PhD, even though the final examination board may not yet have taken place and the overall result is therefore not yet known) OR professional qualifications and experience equivalent to a Master's qualification.
  • Applicants should have applied to study for a PhD at the University of Nottingham before they submit their Wolfson Scholarship application. It is, however, not necessary to have received a formal offer by the point of application.

About the Scholarship

Each Scholarship offers a fixed sum of £114,000 over three years for full-time study or six years for part-time study and covers:

  • Home (UK)/International Tuition Fees (where an International applicant is successful, the Faculty will cover the difference between Home and International fee levels)
  • A maintenance grant (referred to as a stipend) fixed at £28,250 per year (pro rata part-time) which is tax-free and paid monthly
  • A research and training allowance

Definition of eligible subject disciplines

Wolfson Postgraduate Scholarships are in three disciplines that align closely with the Foundation's interests: history, literature, and languages. These are broadly defined, and applicants should note that it is the area of study which is important rather than the name of the academic school/department in which they will be based.

History: as well as broad-based historical and historiographical studies, this may include such areas as classics, music, history of art, visual culture, or architectural history, provided the research is grounded within historical methodology.

Literature (excluding creative writing): as well as literary and textual studies, this may include research that involves critical theory, theatre, film and other visual media, provided there is a literary element within the research (e.g. the translation of literature to screen).

Languages (excluding linguistics): research should be in applied languages other than English. It may involve the study of literary or historical texts, theatre, film or other visual media, translation, or the philosophy of language, provided that the research is focused primarily on a language other than English. N.B. While research can be working with any language, it is expected that the student's final thesis is written in English.

How to apply

Application is through the Arts and Humanities Research Council Doctoral Landscape Award (DLA) application process

  1. Ensure you meet the above eligibility criteria
  2. Go to AHRC studentships
  3. Apply for a Doctoral Landscape Award (DLA) and tick the relevant box to confirm your interest in Wolfson Scholarship funding

Deadline for application: noon (GMT) on 19 January 2027

ESRC White Rose DTP Studentships 2027/28 Overview

The Economic and Social Research Council is the UK's largest funding agency for research and postgraduate training relating to social and economic issues.

The University of Leeds is part of the ESRC White Rose Doctoral Training Partnership, forming a collaboration between the Universities of Leeds, Sheffield, York, Bradford, Sheffield Hallam, Hull and Manchester Metropolitan. Through this, the University is able to offer a range of social science PhD studentships.

The studentship application for these awards for 2027/28 entry will open in September 2026. The deadline for Applications will be: 17:00 (UK Time) 20 January 2027.

Applicants who are interested in the WRDTP Pathway, AQM, ADA and WRDTP/SHF Awards are invited to attend an information session for guidance on the application process. The session will be held online on: Thursday 8 October 2026: 17:30 – 18:30.

Award Types

Studentships are available to UK and international (including EU) applicants in seven named Thematic Interdisciplinary Training Pathways and can be held full-time or part-time for the following award types:

  • +3.5 Studentships: funding for a 3.5-year PhD (for students with a social science Masters degree, and with 60 or more credits of M-level social science research methods training)
  • +3.75 Studentships: funding for an integrated PGCert/PhD (for students who already have a social sciences Masters degree but have fewer than 60 credits of M (Masters) level social science research training)
  • 1+3.5 Studentships: funding for a 1 year Masters programme, followed by the 3.5 year PhD (for students without a social science Masters degree; the Masters programme will deliver the core social sciences research methods training requirements)

Available Studentships

  • WRDTP Pathway Studentships: offer applicants the opportunity to develop proposals for impactful social science research that engages with the key themes and challenges identified in our thematic interdisciplinary pathways.
  • Up to 2 ESRC WRDTP Advanced Quantitative Methods Studentships: for researchers who will use cutting edge quantitative research methods.
  • Up to 2 ESRC Advanced Data Analytics Awards: for researchers who will use cutting edge data analysis techniques or deploy large scale or 'big' data.
  • Up to 2 WRDTP/Stuart Hall Foundation Studentships: available for Black British students.
  • A number of ESRC WRDTP Collaborative Studentships will be available - information will be provided in early Spring 2027.

Duration of the Award

  • 1+3.5 studentships: Full-time (4.5 years) or part-time pro rata
  • +3.5 studentships: Full-time (3.5 years) or part-time pro rata
  • +3.75 studentships: Full-time (3 years 9 months) or part-time pro rata

Full-time awards will be made for one year in the first instance and will be renewed each year, subject to satisfactory academic progress. Part-time awards will be made for 24 months (two calendar years) in the first instance and will be renewed each year, subject to satisfactory academic progress.

Funding

  • The award will cover fees at standard UKRI rates
  • A maintenance grant (£21,805 in Session 2026/27 for full-time study, pro-rata for part-time study). This amount increases per annum in line with the UKRI rate
  • Research Training Support Grant covers travel and research costs during the PhD part of the award
  • This award is open to all applicants, whether Home or International (including EU). Please note that the award does not cover the costs associated with moving to the UK. All such costs (visa costs, Immigration Health Surcharge/medical insurance, flights etc) would have to be met by yourself, or you will need to find an alternative funding source.

Other Conditions

  • Applicants applying on both a 1+3.5, +3.5 and +3.75 basis MUST in the first instance apply for a place on a research postgraduate programme and be in receipt of a Student ID Number to be eligible for an ESRC White Rose DTP Studentship. Applications without a valid ID Number will be rejected.
  • +3.5 and +3.75 awards must be taken up on 1 October 2027; 1+3.5 awards must be taken up in September 2027
  • Applicants must live within a reasonable distance of the University of Leeds whilst in receipt of this Scholarship
  • All WRDTP programmes include an integral 3-month 'Research in Practice' placement as standard
  • Applicants should read the ESRC Postgraduate Funding Guide and be willing to abide by the conditions and regulations therein.

Selection Process

After a School selection process, applicants will be informed as to whether they are being nominated for an ESRC WRDTP Studentship. The White Rose Academic Quality Committee will review the nominations and decide on the final list of awards. The final outcome is expected mid/end April 2027.

How to Apply

Stage 1: First of all apply for a research programme of study by completing the application form. In order to be considered for the scholarship you must submit all the required supporting documents for your application for study. PhD application deadline – You are strongly encouraged to submit your application for a PhD place (Stage 1) by 6 January 2027.

Stage 2: Once you are in receipt of your 9 digit Student Application ID complete the ESRC WRDTP online application form. Before completing the studentship application form, you are strongly advised to read the WRDTP Pathway, AQM and ADA Awards – Guidance for Applicants and the Assessment Criteria.

Entry Requirements

Applicants must meet the entry requirements of their nominating School. The ESRC also stipulates that for all studentships, students must have qualifications of the standard of a good honours degree at first- or upper second-class level, from a UK academic higher education institution, or through a combination of qualifications and/or experience, be able to demonstrate equivalence.

English Language Requirements

The minimum English language entry requirement for research postgraduate research study is an IELTS of 6.0 overall with at least 5.5 in each component (reading, writing, listening and speaking) or equivalent. The test must be dated within two years of the start date of the course in order to be valid. Some schools and faculties have a higher requirement.

Programme Overview

Research in Quantum Technology for Physics develops new experimental techniques and approaches that exploit quantum mechanics to better our understanding of the physical world.

As a postgraduate researcher in this Department of Physics and Astronomy research theme, you could use state-of-the-art laser facilities at the Photon Science Institute and work with industrial partners, depending on your project.

Apply for one of our advertised research projects, or bring your own research question to a supervisor to develop a proposal.

Programme Details

  • Degree: Doctor of Philosophy / Master of Philosophy
  • Duration: PhD 3–4 Years Full-Time, MPhil 1 year Full-Time
  • Study Mode: PhD Full-time: In person; Part-time: In person; MPhil Full-time: In person
  • Year of Entry: 2027

Department

Department of Physics & Astronomy, The University of Manchester.

Programme Description

The Department of Physics and Astronomy at Manchester is one of the largest and most active physics departments in the UK. We have a long tradition of excellence in both teaching and research, and have interests in most areas of contemporary research.

The Department has a strong presence in a number of Manchester-based centres for multidisciplinary research: The National Graphene Institute, the Photon Science Institute, the Manchester Centre for Non-Linear Dynamics, and the Dalton Nuclear Institute. In addition, the Jodrell Bank Observatory in Cheshire is a part of the department.

The Photon Physics group studies the interactions between light and matter and uses light to investigate a range of novel and important systems. The scope of the work ranges from improving our theoretical understanding of the quantum nature of these interactions to developing new spectroscopic and microscopic techniques for material science, medicine and biology.

Our experimental work utilises light in its broadest sense, exploiting the electromagnetic spectrum from x-rays to THz frequencies and we employ the facilities available in the Photon Science Institute as well as developing new light sources ourselves. This work often studies the physical processes that underpin applications with important real-world impact, such as the development of efficient new solar cells and LEDs for low-energy lighting.

The postgraduate research environment is well funded and as demonstrated by our ranking in REF2021. Supervision is provided by academic staff, who are leaders in their fields, with independent pastoral back-up. Transferable skills training is available and there are some school teaching opportunities.

Entry Requirements

The standard academic entry requirement for this PhD is an upper second-class (2:1) honours degree in a discipline directly relevant to the PhD (or international equivalent) OR any upper-second class (2:1) honours degree and a Master's degree at merit in a discipline directly relevant to the PhD (or international equivalent). Other combinations of qualifications and research or work experience may also be considered. Please contact the admissions team to check.

English Language Requirements

All applicants will need to demonstrate competency in English language. Applicants who do not already possess an acceptable English Language qualification will need to take a recognised test and attain a minimum IELTS 6.5 overall with a minimum of 6 in writing and listening, and 5.5 in all other sub-tests. TOEFL iBT: At least 4.5 overall with no subskill below 4.5. We do not accept 'MyBestScore'. Pearson Test of English (PTE): At least 70 overall with no subtest below 59.

Fees and Funding

Fees for entry in 2027 have not yet been set. For reference, the fees for the academic year beginning September 2026 were as follows:

PhD (full-time)
UK students (per annum): Band A - £5,238; Band B - £7,700; Band C - £13,200, Band D - £21,200; Band E £36,100
International, including EU, students (per annum): Band A - £29,900; Band B - £32,400; Band C - £37,900, Band D - £45,900; Band E £60,800

PhD (part-time)
UK students (per annum): Band A - £2,619; Band B - £3,850; Band C - £6,600; Band D - £10,550; Band E - £18,050
International, including EU, students (per annum): Band A - £14,500; Band B - £16,200; Band C - £18,950; Band D - £22,950; Band E - £30,400

The programme fee will vary depending on the cost of running the project. Fees quoted are fully inclusive and, therefore, you will not be required to pay any additional bench fees or administration costs.

There are a range of scholarships, studentships and awards at university, faculty and department level to support both UK and overseas postgraduate researchers.

How to Apply

Before applying we recommend that you read the 'Advice to Applicants' section. When you are ready to apply, follow these instructions.

Apply online. In your application you'll need to include:

  • The name of this programme
  • Your research project title (i.e. the advertised project name or proposed project name) or area of research
  • Your proposed supervisor's name
  • If you already have funding or you wish to be considered for any of the available funding
  • A supporting statement (see 'Advice to Applicants' for what to include)
  • Details of your previous university level study
  • Names and contact details of your two referees.

Advice to Applicants

Before you start your application, you should have:

  • Identified the specific research project, CDT or dual-award you'd like to apply for or, if you already have funding, determined your own research project and title and discussed this with a supervisor.
  • Contacted the project supervisor and spoken to them about your suitability for the project.
  • Browsed funding you are eligible for and discussed this with your supervisor, if you don't already have your own funding.

You'll also need to make sure you have the following:

  • Supporting statement: A one or two page statement outlining your motivation to pursue postgraduate research, the area(s) of research you're interested in, why you want to undertake postgraduate research at Manchester, any relevant research or work experience, the key findings of your previous research experience, and techniques and skills you've developed.
  • Certificates and transcripts: Certificates and final transcripts of any completed university-level qualifications and interim transcripts for qualifications in progress. If your transcripts are in a language other than English, you must provide an official English translation. If your current weighted average mark or GPA is not included on these documents, please also include an official document from your university verifying this information.
  • CV: Summarising your academic record and highlighting experience that demonstrates your potential to conduct research.
  • English language proof: A certificate or evidence demonstrating your English language ability and proficiency. Applications can be considered without this evidence but any offer would be conditional on meeting minimum requirements.
  • Referees: Names and contact details of two academic referees who we can get in contact with and will support your application.

Interview Requirements

An interview is required for entry to this programme of study. Read our interview advice to help you prepare.

PhD Overview

  • University: Monash University
  • Department: Department of Materials Science and Engineering
  • Location: Melbourne, Victoria, Australia
  • Study Level: PhD / Doctoral Research
  • Project Title: Smart Polymer Nanocomposites: Design, Synthesis and Applications
  • Research Area: Polymer Science, Materials Science, Nanotechnology and Nanocomposites

  • Supervisor: Associate Professor Vipul Agarwal
  • International Applicants: Eligible subject to Monash University admission and scholarship requirements
  • Application Status: Applicants should confirm current project and scholarship availability with the supervisor and Monash University before applying.

About the Research Project

The PhD project focuses on the design and development of smart polymer nanocomposites for advanced coating and foam applications.

A major challenge in conventional polymer nanocomposites is achieving effective and controlled dispersion of fillers throughout the polymer matrix. The research will investigate new synthesis approaches for developing polymeric and multidimensional filler nanocomposites with controlled structures and tunable properties.

Particular attention will be given to controlling the interfacial arrangement of multidimensional fillers around polymer particles, including systems formed in oil-water emulsions.

The project will also investigate externally stimuli-responsive polymer nanocomposite coatings and foams.

Potential applications include:

  • sensing technologies;
  • chemical catalysis;
  • corrosion protection;
  • shielding materials;
  • smart coatings; and
  • functional polymer foam technologies.

The work combines polymer science, nanomaterials, surface and interface chemistry, materials synthesis and advanced materials characterisation.

Who Should Apply?

The opportunity is particularly relevant to applicants with an academic or research background in areas such as:

  • Chemistry;
  • Polymer Chemistry;
  • Materials Science;
  • Materials Engineering;
  • Nanotechnology;
  • Polymer Science; or
  • closely related disciplines.

Candidates are expected to demonstrate strong academic performance and research potential.

Relevant laboratory experience may include:

  • polymer synthesis;
  • nanoparticle synthesis;
  • nanocomposite fabrication;
  • materials characterisation;
  • polymer or nanoparticle analytical techniques; and
  • experimental materials research.

Strong scientific writing skills and the ability to conduct research independently and collaboratively are also valuable.

Peer-reviewed research publications, particularly strong first-author publications, may make an applicant more competitive, although applicants must ultimately satisfy Monash University's formal admission and scholarship criteria.

Monash University PhD Entry Requirements

For standard PhD admission, Monash University normally requires one of the following:

  • a relevant bachelor's degree of at least four years that includes a research thesis or research project, with results equivalent to at least Australian Second Class Honours Division A (2A);
  • a relevant master's degree containing a substantial research thesis or project equivalent to at least 25% of one year of full-time study, with results equivalent to at least Second Class Honours Division A; or
  • another qualification and relevant experience considered equivalent by Monash University's Graduate Research Committee.

Meeting the minimum PhD admission requirements does not automatically guarantee a scholarship. Research scholarships at Monash are competitive and take into account academic achievement, research experience and research outputs.

English Language Requirements

International applicants must satisfy Monash University's graduate research English language proficiency requirements.

Evidence may be provided through an approved English-language test or, in eligible cases, previous tertiary education undertaken entirely in English.

Applicants should check the current Monash Graduate Research English Language Proficiency requirements before submitting their application because accepted tests, score requirements and validity conditions may change.

Scholarship and Funding

The advertised project has been promoted as a fully funded 3.5-year PhD opportunity.

For centrally managed Monash graduate research scholarships, the standard 2026 RTP Stipend and Monash Graduate Scholarship rate is AUD $37,145 per year for full-time students.

Depending on the scholarship awarded, funding may include:

  • a living allowance/stipend;
  • relocation allowance where applicable; and
  • tuition-fee support for eligible students.

For international students, Monash also offers tuition scholarships that may be packaged with a stipend scholarship. The Monash International Tuition Scholarship can cover course tuition fees and a single Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) policy.

Applicants should note that the exact funding package attached to an individual research project must be confirmed with Monash University or the project supervisor.

Supervisor

The project is associated with Associate Professor Vipul Agarwal in the Department of Materials Science and Engineering at Monash University.

His research profile lists the following PhD projects:

  • Smart polymer nanocomposites: design, synthesis and applications
  • Sustainable recycled three-dimensional polymer nanocomposites

His Monash University profile currently indicates that he is accepting PhD students.

How to Apply

Applicants should first review the project and contact the prospective supervisor where required by the Faculty of Engineering.

A typical Monash graduate research application involves:

  1. checking eligibility for the PhD program;
  2. identifying and contacting an appropriate research supervisor;
  3. preparing the required research and academic documentation;
  4. providing evidence of English-language proficiency;
  5. obtaining a faculty invitation to apply where required; and
  6. submitting the PhD and scholarship application through Monash University's graduate research application system.

Graduate research admission and scholarship applications are normally submitted through the Monash myApp portal.

Eligible applicants applying through the central graduate research scholarship process are automatically considered for applicable Monash graduate research scholarships rather than having to submit a separate application for every scholarship.

Documents Typically Required

Applicants should prepare relevant documents such as:

  • academic transcripts;
  • degree certificates;
  • curriculum vitae (CV);
  • research proposal where required;
  • evidence of previous research experience;
  • publications or research outputs where applicable;
  • English-language proficiency evidence;
  • scholarship or sponsorship documentation where relevant; and
  • any additional documents requested by the university.

2026 RTP rate: the full-time RTP stipend is A$34,315 per year, tax-free, indexed annually.

Simons-Ramanujan Fellowship Overview

This fellowship scheme, generously funded by the Simons Foundation, offers the opportunity for promising early career researchers living and working in low and middle-income countries to attend an INI programme as an academic visitor for one to three months. Fellows will be expected to participate in programme activities, which vary by programme, but may include seminars, workshops, and collaborative working. The visit to the programme will be an opportunity for Fellows to develop their own research and forge new connections.

Ramanujan Fellowships History

The fellowship is named after Srinivasa Ramanujan, a highly gifted Indian mathematician of the early 20th century, who was invited to Cambridge in 1914 by G H Hardy. Even though he had little formal training, he is recognised as having had a significant impact on several areas of mathematics.

What does the fellowship offer?

A Ramanujan fellowship will provide the recipient with accommodation, a £25 per diem and up to £1200 for travel to INI.

Fellows with caring responsibilities may apply for an additional allowance of up to £75 per day for housing and childcare costs.

Please note – Fellows will be academic visitors of the Isaac Newton Institute, not employees.

Eligibility

  • Ramanujan Fellowships are open to applicants who reside in a low or middle-income country according to the International Mathematical Union (IMU) classification
  • Fellows can stay between 1-3 months
  • Applicants should be in at least the 3rd year of their PhD

Eligible Programmes

2027:

  • Frontiers in harmonic analysis, elliptic and parabolic PDEs, and GMT (FHA) - January to April 2027
  • Optimal transport (OPT) - January to June 2027

Application process

You will be required to provide your CV with a list of publications, a cover letter and two new academic letters of support, one of these from your home institution. For clarity, an academic letter of support should be written by an academic who is familiar with the applicant’s research activity.

You can attach these documents to the application form.

  1. Fellows can apply for a visit for 1–3 months.
  2. Travel must be by the most economical means, and all travel must be standard class.

University of Glasgow Sanctuary Scholarship Overview

The University of Glasgow Sanctuary Scholarship has been created to support applicants with Refugee or Asylum Seeker status who are currently living in the UK and hold an offer to study with us in the 2027/28 academic year. The scholarship is open to prospective undergraduate and postgraduate taught students at the University of Glasgow applying for entry in September 2027/28. Please note that you must have applied to the University before submitting an application for this scholarship.

As a University of Sanctuary, we are committed to ensuring that those with the ambition and determination to pursue higher education have the opportunity to do so. This scholarship provides a full tuition fee waiver along with financial support for living costs, helping recipients focus on their studies and thrive both academically and personally.

Through this initiative, we aim to offer meaningful opportunities to talented individuals seeking sanctuary, enabling them to rebuild their futures and become part of our global #TeamUofG community.

Scholarship Value

The Sanctuary Scholarship provides:

  • Full tuition fee waiver for the duration of study, where you are not eligible to apply for mainstream student finance to cover full tuition fees
  • £5,000 per year towards study costs

The scholarship will meet the cost of tuition fees for the duration of your programme, for applicants who are unable to access mainstream funding through Student Awards Agency Scotland (SAAS) or Student Finance.

This scholarship is not available to PGdip, PDGE or part-time programmes.

Undergraduate Students

Undergraduate students with refugee status (or equivalent) and access to funding are eligible to apply for the scholarship and would receive the £5,000 stipend towards study costs only, if successful.

Postgraduate Taught Masters Students

Postgraduate Taught Masters students with refugee status (or equivalent) and access to funding are eligible to apply for the scholarship and would receive the £5,000 stipend towards study costs and a partial tuition fee waiver, to cover any shortfall not met by your Postgraduate Masters tuition fee loan.

Eligibility Criteria

To be eligible applicants must:

  • Hold a firm conditional or unconditional offer for full-time study at the University of Glasgow for 2027/28
  • Currently be located in the United Kingdom and have Home or RUK fee status
  • Have submitted a claim for asylum in the UK OR are actively appealing a negative decision on a claim for asylum in the UK OR have been granted Refugee Status, Humanitarian Protection (HP) or Discretionary Leave (DL) by the Home Office, as a result of an asylum claim
  • OR have come to the UK through schemes such as:
  • UK Resettlement Scheme (UKRS)
  • Afghan citizens Resettlement Scheme
  • Afghan Relocations and Assistance Policy (ARAP)
  • Syrian Vulnerable Persons Resettlement Scheme (VPRS)
  • Ukraine Sponsorship Scheme (Homes for Ukraine)
  • Ukraine Family Scheme

Please note that you must have applied to the University before submitting an application for this scholarship.

If you are unsure of whether you are eligible to apply, please contact the team using the enquiry form.

Required Documentation

Applications CANNOT be considered without the relevant documentation to support them:

If you are subject to Home Office Temporary Admission/Immigration Bail Reporting, please provide your:

  • Application Registration Card (ARC) or Biometric Residence Permit (BRP) – Front AND Back
  • Immigration Bail Reporting Notice (this may also be referred to as a Temporary Admission Document or BAIL 201) – please include every page of this document.

OR

If you are not subject to Home Office Temporary Admission/Immigration Bail Reporting, please provide your:

  • Application Registration Card (ARC) or Biometric Residence Permit (BRP) – Front AND Back
  • The most recent documentation you have received from the Home Office in conjunction with your application/appeal – this should show your Home Office reference number.

OR

  • A share code provided by the UK government that can prove your right to study in the UK. You may have access to a share code if you have an e-visa.

Important eVisa Information

If you have a BRP expiring on 31st December 2025, but your overall visa permission is longer than this, you must take action now. More information can be found via the University's immigration compliance team (immigrationcompliance@glasgow.ac.uk).

Number of Scholarships

6

Additional Information

Should your immigration status change part way through your studies, you should inform the Scholarships Team as soon as possible, as this may affect your eligibility for the scholarship. Changes to immigration status will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis. The scholarship funding will not cease automatically but may be recalculated.

Please note that University accommodation is not included in the Sanctuary Scholarship. Applicants will therefore need to cover their own accommodation costs or already live within a reasonable commuting distance of the University.

We also have a small number of donor-funded scholarships, which cover the £5,000 stipend only. Please note that by submitting an application for the Sanctuary scholarships, you will also be considered for the donor-funded awards.

How to Apply

Applications for this scholarship for the 2027-28 academic session will open soon. In the meantime, please provide your details and we will be in touch when the scholarship is open for applications.

description:
Scholarship Overview

The Sir James McNeill Postgraduate Research Scholarship (SJMN) is a full-funded graduate research scholarship at Monash University, awarded every two years. The 2026 application deadline is 31 October 2026. The scholarship is available for Research Doctorate (PhD) and Research Masters programs at Monash University's Melbourne campuses. Eligible faculties are Arts (School of Music only), Engineering, Medicine/Nursing/Health Sciences, and Science.

Benefits & Coverage

  • Living allowance (stipend) of approximately AUD $4,467 per month, totalling AUD $53,608 per year (2026 rate).
  • Full tuition fee coverage (Research Training Program fee offset).
  • Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) for international students.
  • Relocation allowance (if eligible) for interstate or overseas relocation.
  • Research allowance for thesis and research costs.
  • Professional development opportunities.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Citizenship: Australian citizen, New Zealand citizen, Australian permanent resident, Australian humanitarian visa holder, or international student (no nationality restriction).
  • Research must be environmentally responsible and socially beneficial.
  • Must meet Monash's competitive scholarship selection process requirements.
  • Must meet English language proficiency requirements (IELTS/TOEFL/PTE).
  • Must be enrolled full-time in a Research Master's or PhD program.

Application Process

  1. Choose your research area and identify a potential supervisor using Monash's "Find a Supervisor" tool.
  2. Create an account on the myApp Portal (Monash's official graduate research application portal).
  3. Submit the Graduate Research Admission + Scholarship application with: research proposal, academic transcripts (certified copies), degree certificates, English proficiency proof, academic CV (max 2 pages), and contact details of 2 referees.
  4. Submit by 31 October 2026 (Round 4 closing).

Scholarship Overview

The Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarships are , fully funded scholarships offered by Delft University of Technology (TU Delft) for exceptional international students. Application Process (Step-by-Step)

  1. Create an account on the TU Delft MSc portal

title: EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships 2027 - Fully Funded Life Sciences Research in Europe
stipend: Salary or stipend (rates vary by country) plus relocation
deadlineText: Open - Apply as soon as possible

organization.name: EMBO (European Molecular Biology Organization)
organization.about: EMBO, the European Molecular Biology Organization, supports life sciences researchers through fellowships, training, scientific meetings and professional networks. Its programmes help researchers develop careers and exchange knowledge across institutions and countries. EMBO also publishes scientific research, connecting the international life sciences community with resources for collaboration, learning and scholarly communication.

intro: EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships support excellent postdoctoral researchers in the life sciences for up to two years. International mobility is a key requirement. Includes salary, relocation allowance, and child support. Applications accepted throughout the year with cutoff dates. Next deadline: 22 January 2027.
description:
Programme Overview

EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships support excellent postdoctoral researchers throughout Europe and the world for a period of up to two years. International mobility is a key requirement. The fellowship includes a salary or stipend, a relocation allowance and support for fellows with children. Awardees can attend an EMBO Laboratory Leadership course and become part of the global network of EMBO Fellows.

Eligibility Criteria

  • PhD Degree: Applicants must hold a PhD degree or equivalent at the start of the fellowship, but not necessarily at the time the application is submitted.
  • PhD Recency: Applicants who already hold a PhD degree are eligible if they obtained their PhD degree within the two years preceding the application submission date. The Fellowship Office considers the submission date of the application to check if the applicant holds a PhD title for less than 2 years.
  • Career Breaks: Exceptions to the recency rule are made for applicants with career breaks during the relevant period due to parental leave (one year per child for female scientists; three months per child or total paternal leave taken for male scientists), mandatory military/civil service, or extraordinary personal circumstances such as severe illness or full-time care of an ill family member. Applicants must contact the Fellowship office prior to submission to obtain an exception.
  • Medical Degree: Candidates with a medical degree (M.D.) may be eligible to apply provided they hold a PhD (MD-PhD programme).
  • Publications: Applicants must have at least one first (or joint first) author primary research paper accepted for publication or published in an international peer-reviewed journal at the time the application is submitted. A first-author preprint with public in-depth peer reviews (e.g., from Peer Community In, Review Commons) is also sufficient.
  • Mobility: EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships are intended to promote international exchange. All applications must involve a change of country. Specific rules apply for applications to work in EMBC Member States, EMBC/EMBO global partners, and Non-EMBC Member States. Applicants wishing to work in the country where they obtained their PhD are NOT eligible.
  • Scientific Scope: Research proposals must be within EMBO's scientific scope (life sciences). Applications are expected to be driven by a biological question, explore mechanisms behind biological phenomena, and yield biological insight. Applied or clinical work without a clear biological question is not eligible.

Funding and Benefits

  • Salary or stipend (rates vary by country).
  • Relocation allowance (amount varies by country).
  • Support for fellows with children (child daycare and dependent child allowances).
  • Parental leave (extension of fellowship duration).
  • Long-term sick leave extensions.
  • Training in lab leadership and access to the extensive network of other EMBO Fellows.
  • Travel and relocation support as a lump sum before the start date.

Application Process

Applications for an EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowship are accepted via the EMBO online application system. There are no application deadlines, but there are two cutoff evaluation dates:

  • Spring Evaluation: Second Friday of February, 2 PM CET. Results announced at the end of June.
  • Autumn Evaluation: Second Friday of July, 2 PM CEST. Results announced at the end of December.

The date on which the candidate confirms that their application is complete is the reference date for eligibility and evaluation. Only fully completed applications will be considered.

description:
Fellowship Overview

The Luxembourg Centre for Contemporary and Digital History (C²DH) is the University of Luxembourg's third interdisciplinary research centre, focusing on high-quality research, analysis and public dissemination in the field of contemporary history. It promotes an interdisciplinary approach with a particular focus on new digital methods and tools for historical research and teaching. The C²DH offers one short-term fellowship position for 2 months for a scholar at risk, including Palestine and Sudan.

Fellowship Benefits

  • Monthly reimbursement of EUR 1,200 for accommodation.
  • Monthly reimbursement of EUR 1,800 for daily costs.
  • The funding is supposed to cover all expenses including travel and insurance.
  • Office space and other relevant facilities provided by C²DH.
  • Fellows are expected to reside in Luxembourg or the Greater Region and will arrange their own accommodation.
  • Fellowship holder will be assigned to one of our Research departments and asked to present their current project in a seminar or colloquium.

Eligibility Criteria

Following criteria established by the Scholars at Risk network, at-risk scholars are those who are experiencing, or experienced very recently, direct risk, such as threat of violence/harm to the individual, harassment/intimidation, threat of arrest/imprisonment, etc, or they are experiencing general physical risk from an active conflict in their country of origin that hinder them from fully and freely exercising their research and academic work.

Applicants are expected to pursue their own research, which can relate to any region in the world and is ideally related to contemporary, public or digital history, broadly understood.

  • Public History and Outreach
  • Contemporary History of Europe
  • Digital History and Historiography

description:
Programme Overview

MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships enhance the creative and innovative potential of researchers holding a PhD who wish to acquire new skills through advanced training, international, interdisciplinary and inter-sectoral mobility. The scheme is open to excellent researchers of any nationality. It also encourages researchers to work on research and innovation projects in the non-academic sector and is open to researchers wishing to reintegrate in Europe, to those who are displaced by conflict, as well as to researchers with high potential who are seeking to restart their careers in research.

Fellowship Types

  • European Postdoctoral Fellowships: Open to researchers of any nationality who wish to engage in R&I projects by either coming to Europe from any country in the world or moving within Europe. Standard duration: 12 to 24 months.
  • Global Postdoctoral Fellowships: Open to European nationals or long-term residents who wish to engage in R&I projects with organisations outside EU Member States and Horizon Europe Associated Countries. Requires an outgoing phase of minimum 12 and maximum 24 months in a non-associated Third Country, and a mandatory 12-month return phase to a host organisation based in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country.

Funding and Benefits

  • Living allowance: €6,350 per month (gross salary).
  • Mobility allowance: €710 per month.
  • Family allowance: €660 per month (if applicable).
  • Research, training, and networking costs: €1,000 per month.
  • Approximately 1,600 fellowships available, covering two years of salary and around €50,000 in research project funds.
  • Total indicative budget: EUR 388.57 million.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Must hold a PhD at the time of the deadline for applications.
  • Maximum of 8 years full-time equivalent (FTE) experience in research, measured from the date of award of the first doctoral degree.
  • Open to researchers of any nationality.
  • Must undertake international mobility (coming to Europe from any country or moving within Europe).
  • Applications are made jointly by the researcher and a beneficiary in the academic or non-academic sector.
  • Specific eligibility conditions apply to MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships in the research areas covered by the Euratom Research and Training Programme 2026-2027.

Application Process

Applications are submitted via the EU Funding & Tenders Portal and are split into two parts (Part A and Part B). The application form specific to this call is available in the Submission System. Full details are available on the call page on the EU Funding & Tenders portal.

organization.about: University of Oxford is a collegiate research university in Oxford, England. It offers undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral education across medicine, science, engineering, humanities and social sciences. Its departments, colleges and research institutes support scholarship and international collaboration, providing opportunities for students and researchers to investigate questions across many academic fields.

intro: The DPhil in Cardiovascular Science (Cardiovascular Disease Prevention) at Oxford is a four-year programme funded by the British Heart Foundation. It combines interdisciplinary training with research at the intersection of population health, systems biology, and data science/AI. Final application deadline: 1 December 2026.
description:
Programme Overview

The DPhil in Cardiovascular Science (Collaborative Vision for Cardiovascular Disease (CVD) Prevention) is a collaboration between the University of Oxford, the University of Cambridge, the University of Edinburgh, and Imperial College London. This four-year DPhil course combines interdisciplinary training with in-depth research. You will be trained to work at the intersection of population health, systems biology, and data science/AI, combining expertise across these fields to tackle one of the most pressing challenges in global health. By harnessing large-scale multimodal data and emerging technologies, you will develop new approaches to understand, predict, and prevent heart and circulatory diseases.

Research Areas and Structure

Students will be based in one of the following institutes: Oxford (2 studentships), Cambridge (5 studentships), Edinburgh (2 studentships), and Imperial (1 studentship) while benefiting from training, co-supervision, and collaboration across the partner institutions. Projects will span a range of topics including health data science, AI and machine learning, multi-omics, epidemiology, and translational cardiovascular research. You will be part of a cohort-based programme, gaining access to shared training activities, collaborative networks, and state-of-the-art data resources across the multi-institute partnership.

Year One

In year one, you will take an induction programme, training courses and research rotations before selecting your DPhil project and supervisory team (all at your host institution). Please note that it is not possible to change institution between years 1 and 2, except under exceptional circumstances.

Years Two to Four

In years two-four, you will carry out your DPhil research with interdisciplinary supervision. Additional opportunities will include advanced training courses, programme-wide workshops and symposia, and optional placements with academic or industry partners, including EMBL-European Bioinformatics Institute, Wellcome Sanger Institute, AstraZeneca, Novo Nordisk, Genomics Ltd, Owlstone Medical, ThermoFischer Scientific, and Flagship Pioneering.

Funding and Costs

This DPhil includes funding support from the British Heart Foundation (BHF). Funding and costs information relates to entry in 2027-28. Annual course fees and living costs are covered for successful applicants.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Standard level English language requirement.
  • A first-class or strong upper second-class undergraduate degree with honours in a relevant discipline.
  • A master's degree is desirable but not essential.
  • Proven and potential academic excellence.
  • References (three overall, academic preferred).
  • Supporting documents including official transcripts and a statement of purpose (maximum 500 words).

Application Process

This course has a two-stage application process:

  1. Stage 1: Apply to the University of Cambridge – You must first apply to Cambridge. The final application deadline for entry in 2027-28 is 12:00 midday UK time on Tuesday, 1 December 2026.
  2. Stage 2: Apply to the University of Oxford – If you are successful at Stage 1, you will be invited to complete a University of Oxford application. The application fee is waived for all applications to this course.

description:

Computer science research at The University of Manchester builds on a legacy that includes the world's first stored-program computer, spanning major advances in AI and advanced computing systems. As a postgraduate researcher, you will work within the Department of Computer Science, based in the Kilburn Building, on research addressing global challenges from the foundations and technologies of computer science to enabling responsible AI and using big data for societal benefit.

Core Computer Science research is augmented by interdisciplinary research taking place at the interface with discipline areas including mathematics, physics, medicine, biology, and engineering.

intro: Two fully funded PhD positions are available in the Laboratory for Multiscale Geomechanics at McMaster University. Research at the intersection of continuum mechanics, computational mechanics, constitutive modelling, and geomechanics. Rolling review until filled.
description:
Programme Overview

Two fully funded PhD positions are available in the Laboratory for Multiscale Geomechanics in the Department of Civil Engineering at McMaster University. Preferred start dates: January 2027 or September 2027. Some flexibility may be possible. The positions are particularly suitable for candidates interested in mechanics-based modelling, numerical implementation, and the fundamental behaviour of soils, rocks, granular materials, or other geomaterials.

Research Focus

Our group develops advanced computational and theoretical methods for understanding the behaviour of geomaterials across multiple spatial scales and under coupled physical processes. Our research lies at the intersection of:

  • Continuum and solid mechanics
  • Computational mechanics and numerical methods
  • Constitutive modelling
  • Multiscale mechanics
  • Geomechanics

Potential research topics include large-deformation modeling of geostructures, thermo-hydro-mechanical modeling of geomaterials, and small-scale simulations of porous multiphase materials.

Funding and Benefits

  • $21,000 CAD/year studentship.
  • Competitive scholarships will be additional.
  • Fully funded PhD positions.
  • Access to state-of-the-art research facilities at McMaster University.
  • Opportunity to contribute to a growing research program in computational geomechanics.

Eligibility Criteria

  • A degree in civil engineering, mechanical engineering, materials engineering, or a closely related field.
  • Strong preparation in continuum mechanics, solid mechanics, computational mechanics, numerical methods, or a related area.
  • Evidence of research potential through a thesis, research project, publication, technical report, software development, or comparable experience.
  • An interest in applying mechanics and computational methods to geomechanics.
  • Previous research experience in geomechanics is an asset but is not required.
  • Experience implementing numerical methods such as FEM, DEM, MPM, SPH, or molecular dynamics (MD) is beneficial but not required.

Application Process

Please email the following materials to eghbalm@mcmaster.ca:

  1. A curriculum vitae.
  2. Unofficial academic transcripts.
  3. A statement of no more than 500 words describing your research interests, relevant preparation, the types of problems you would like to investigate, and how this opportunity aligns with your academic goals.

The PhD project centers on a fundamental question in molecular biology: How is human translation controlled at the structural level?

organization.about: The Ghedini Lab at Monash University in Melbourne, Australia, studies community ecology and evolution. intro: The Ghedini Lab at Monash University is recruiting a PhD candidate to study how organismal physiology underpins community stability in marine phytoplankton. Part of the international ReDiLEEP Doctoral Network. Fully funded Monash PhD scholarship. Deadline: 30 October 2026. Applicants must apply separately for and obtain a Monash PhD scholarship; funding is not automatically attached to this project.
description:
Project Overview

The Community Ecology & Evolution lab led by Dr Giulia Ghedini at Monash University invites applications for a Doctoral Candidate position within the Marie Sklodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network ReDiLEEP. This is an exciting opportunity to study how organismal physiology underpins community stability, collaborating with other PhD students and research groups in Europe to understand how species in an ecosystem respond to changes and the importance of variation in their responses for ecosystem stability.

Research Project DC13: Physiological Basis and Consequences of Response Diversity

The Doctoral Candidate will investigate the physiological basis of response diversity in marine phytoplankton communities. This project will develop a mechanistic understanding of response diversity by studying how the variation and evolution of species physiology propagate through species interactions to stabilise ecological communities to global change. The Doctoral Candidate will use theory-informed laboratory experiments, physiological and eco-evolutionary assays, to test how differences in species energy use drive species persistence and recovery under global change and how these responses support community stability.

Funding and Benefits

  • Full-time PhD opportunity at Monash University (subject to securing a scholarship).
  • Monash Graduate Scholarship covering tuition fees and a living stipend.
  • Stipend of AUD $37,145 per year (2026 rate), tax-free if there is no other income.
  • Typically includes a relocation allowance.
  • Membership in the ReDiLEEP international doctoral network.
  • Opportunities for international collaboration with researchers in Europe and Japan.
  • Up to 6 months of secondments at universities in Belgium, the UK, and Germany.
  • Training in R/Tidyverse, machine learning and AI, data management, visualisation, science-policy communication, and other research skills.
  • Access to Monash research facilities, including marine research, microscopy, flow cytometry, and the Australian Synchrotron.

Eligibility Criteria

  • A motivated researcher with a keen interest in community ecology.
  • Bachelor's degree with First Class Honours or equivalent grades for Master's Degree in biology, ecology, marine biology, environmental sciences, or a closely related field.
  • A peer-reviewed publication (particularly as first author) is not essential but will strongly increase chances of securing a scholarship.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.
  • A demonstrated capacity to work independently and as part of a team.
  • High level of motivation and enthusiasm for the research topic and to perform laboratory work.
  • Experience in statistical analysis in R (or similar software).
  • Open to applicants of all nationalities.
  • Must meet Monash University PhD scholarship eligibility criteria, including English language requirements.

Application Process

Step 1: Submit your application in English by 30 September 2026 as a single PDF file via email to Giulia Ghedini (giulia.ghedini@monash.edu). Applications should include:

  • A cover letter describing your motivation for the position, relevant experience, and fit with DC13 (max 2 pages).
  • A curriculum vitae with details of any publications.
  • Copies of degree certificates and transcripts.
  • Contact details of two referees.

Step 2: Only with the support of the main supervisor, you can apply via the How to Apply page on Monash's website.

The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship Program offers a three-year program designed to train engaged leaders with the skills required to turn their ideas into actions and contribute concretely to addressing the challenges of their communities, Canada, and the world. The Foundation welcomes applications from candidates across a wide range of disciplines in the humanities and social sciences, in business schools, public health, and law.

Scholarship Value

  • Annual stipend of up to $50,000 per year for three years to cover tuition and living expenses.
  • Annual allowance of up to $20,000 per year for three years to support research, networking, and travel related to the doctoral project and Foundation programming.
  • Membership in a dynamic community of Scholars, Mentors, and Fellows.
  • Lifelong membership in the Foundation's alumni network, which includes over 500 individuals.
  • Total value: Up to $210,000 over three years.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Field of study must be broadly related to the humanities or social sciences and address issues relevant to Canada's future.
  • PhD research must align with at least one of the Foundation's four themes: Human Rights and Dignity; Responsible Citizenship; Canada and the World; People and their Natural Environment.

Application Process (Two-Step)

Required Documents

Evaluation Criteria

intro: PRISM (PhD Research Programme for International Training in Sustainable Soft Matter) offers up to 14 fully funded PhD fellowships at PSL University in Paris. Projects focus on eco-friendly chemical processes, circular economy, renewable energies, and carbon capture. Application deadline: 31 October 2026.
description:
Programme Overview

The PRISM (PhD Research Programme for International Training in Sustainable Soft Matter) programme has launched its first call for applications, offering up to 14 fully funded PhD fellowships starting from 1 March 2027 at Paris Sciences & Lettres (PSL) University. The programme trains researchers to address ecological transition challenges through sustainable soft matter science, with projects focused on eco-friendly chemical processes, circular economy, renewable energies, and carbon capture, storage, and valorisation. Co-funded by the European Union under Horizon Europe MSCA COFUND (Grant Agreement 101261637) and partner institutions, PRISM provides interdisciplinary, international, and intersectoral training, including mobility opportunities, secondments, and courses in sustainability, innovation, entrepreneurship, career development, and transferable skills.

Research Themes

PRISM is structured around 4 major scientific themes:

  • T1 – Development of eco-friendly chemical processes
  • T2 – Building a circular economy
  • T3 – Innovative concepts for renewable energy
  • T4 – Carbon capture, storage and valorisation

The PhD projects cross the frontiers between soft matter, microfluidics, chemistry, physics, biology, and materials science.

Available PhD Projects

  • AIM-CO₂: AI-assisted high-pressure microfluidics for CO₂ capture, transport and utilization (Engineering)
  • BUBBLE-AFM: Molecular processes at electrode/electrolyte interfaces during water electrolysis (Physics)
  • NWARPS: Nucleation, Wetting, Adhesion, and Rheology of Polymeric Surfaces (Physics)
  • ROOTSTOCK: Plant root development affected by soil mechanical stresses (Physics)
  • RubisCO.2: Engineering new RubisCOs with increased CO2 catalytic activity (Physics)
  • CAPTURE: Development of Smart Materials for Reversible Low-Energy CO₂ Capture (Chemistry)
  • Micado: Microdroplet catalysis of CO₂-amine C-N bond formation (Chemistry)
  • PlasticPhase: Micro- and Nanoplastics as Modulators of Phase Separation and Protein Aggregation (Chemistry)
  • POAT-CO2-V: Plasma-driven Oxygen Atom Transfer for CO₂ Valorisation (Chemistry)
  • SMART-HAIR: Sustainable Multifunctional Adaptable Responsive Treatment for Hair (Chemistry)
  • SOFTMAT4MET: Functional Soft Matter for Sustainable and Selective Extraction of Critical Metals (Chemistry)
  • STREAM: Seawater Treatment for CO2 Removal via Electrochemical Microelectrode Arrays (Chemistry)
  • UltraHighResNMR: Ultra-high resolution proton NMR at no cost (Chemistry)
  • WISELY: New Chemistries for the Design of Recyclable Polymers (Chemistry)

Candidates may apply to up to five PhD projects before the application deadline.

Salary and Benefits

  • Competitive salary above the national average for PhD candidates in France.
  • Approximate net monthly salary of €2,200.
  • Additional family and mobility allowances available for eligible fellows.
  • Employer's benefits include remote working opportunities, access to sports and leisure activities, free access to public Paris city council's swimming pools, access to CROUS canteen, scientific campus in central Paris, professional development programs, well-being workshops, social benefits through CNAS, partial health insurance support, and 75% support for sustainable mobility.
  • All PRISM doctoral candidates will be employed by ESPCI Paris, regardless of the host laboratory.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Must possess a Master's degree or equivalent/postgraduate degree which formally entitles them to start a doctorate. All applicants with a doctoral degree are ineligible.
  • Minimum English proficiency level of C1 (Advanced) required for applicants from non-English-speaking countries. No French language skills required.
  • Must fulfil the transnational mobility rule: open to all nationalities but all incoming applicants must not have resided or carried out their main activity in France for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to the call for applications deadline.
  • Must be available to start the program on 1 March 2027.
  • Completeness of the application, submitted in English on the PRISM dedicated website, before the deadline of 31 October 2026.

Selection Process

  • Eligibility checks to ensure administrative compliance.
  • Remote evaluation of each application by different reviewers.
  • Interview and selection of shortlisted applicants via videoconference (presentation and questions).
  • Recruitment: once selected, the management team initiates the recruitment process. For some nationalities, mandatory security clearance procedure will be launched at the final stage.
