organization.about: The Cologne Graduate School of Ageing Research provides structured doctoral training in Germany focused on the biology of ageing. It connects partner universities and research institutes in Cologne. Doctoral researchers investigate mechanisms related to ageing and health through supervised projects, scientific training and collaboration across an international biomedical research community.

intro: The Cologne Graduate School of Ageing Research offers up to 12 fully funded PhD positions in ageing research at Germany's leading ageing research cluster. Three-year contracts with TV-L E13 salary. Application deadline: 3 November 2026.
description:
Programme Overview

The Cologne Graduate School of Ageing Research (CGA) in Germany is a joint venture of the University of Cologne Excellence Cluster on Stress Responses in Aging Associated Diseases (CECAD), the University Hospital Cologne, the Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing, and the Max Planck Institute for Metabolism Research. Cologne has emerged as a leading global research cluster with a stellar constellation of institutes and scientists dedicated to ageing research in Life Sciences. Up to 12 fully funded PhD positions are available for the 2027 cohort.

Research Areas

Our international, interdisciplinary faculty offers positions in cell or molecular biology, biochemistry, biophysics, bioinformatics, bioengineering, pharmacology, neuroscience, medical biology, translational medicine, or related fields.

What We Offer

  • An outstanding international research environment at one of Europe's most ageing research clusters, comprising 49 interdisciplinary research groups.
  • Initial work contracts of at least three years with payment based on the German TV-L E13 scale, 65% or on an equivalently remunerated PhD support contract of the Max Planck Society.
  • Dedicated supervision with academic guidance from thesis advisory committees.
  • Comprehensive PhD programme in the vibrant city of Cologne, conducted in English.
  • Individual career mentoring and coaching, wide range of methodology and soft skills courses.
  • Annual conference travel grants.
  • Intensive support and guidance for international students in all administrative matters.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Applicants with an MSc or equivalent degree in Biology, Cell/Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Bioengineering, Bioinformatics, Biophysics, Genetics, Medical Biology, Translational Medicine, or related fields.
  • Students with excellent academic performance in their BSc and MSc studies and a clear interest in the above-mentioned research areas, with strong motivation for ageing research.
  • Candidates with very good English skills (C1 level, written and spoken).
  • Applicants holding a medical degree are encouraged to apply, provided they demonstrate adequate relevant research experience.

Selection Procedure

  • Candidates will be evaluated based on their academic qualifications, research accomplishments, and motivation.
  • Up to 80 candidates will be selected to participate in online panel interviews scheduled for December 2026.
  • From these, up to 25 candidates will be invited to attend the recruitment week in Cologne in February 2027.
  • The PhD positions are anticipated to commence between July and October 2027.
  • All successful applicants will be enrolled through the University of Cologne.

Application Requirements

  • Statements regarding prior research experience and motivation for joining the programme.
  • Detailed research proposal outlining scientific interests and ideas.
  • Specification of three possible host laboratories.
  • Contact details of two academic advisors as referees (one should be your most recent supervisor).
  • CV, certificates, transcripts, and other supporting documents as separate PDF files.
  • Proficiency in both written and spoken English at a C1 level is essential. Submission of a formal language test certificate is not mandatory; alternatively, you may include a written statement outlining your reasons for considering yourself fluent in English.

intro: The Max Planck School of Biomedical AI (BMAI) offers 25 fully funded three-year PhD positions at leading German research institutions. Interdisciplinary research at the interface of AI and life sciences. Application deadline: 1 December 2026.
description:
Programme Overview

The Max Planck School of Biomedical AI (BMAI) offers a three-year interdisciplinary PhD programme at the interface of artificial intelligence and the life sciences. The programme brings together leading researchers from universities and research institutions across Germany and provides doctoral researchers with an international and highly interdisciplinary research environment. 25 fully funded PhD positions are available for the first BMAI cohort starting September 2027.

Research Areas

BMAI develops computational and AI methods across four interconnected research areas:

  • Understanding Molecular and Cellular Systems
  • Protein and Molecule Design
  • Learning Complex Biological Traits from Multi-Scale Data
  • Neural Network Exploration

Funding & Benefits

  • Fully funded PhD positions with competitive employment contracts at participating universities and research institutions.
  • Supervision by two BMAI Fellows.
  • International network of leading universities and research institutions across Germany.
  • Recurring one-week Schools with advanced interdisciplinary courses, scientific exchange, and career development.
  • Access to state-of-the-art research environments across participating institutions.
  • Support for annual participation in an international scientific conference.
  • Structured mentoring and professional development.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Highly motivated and academically excellent candidates who will hold a Master's degree (M.Sc. or equivalent) by September of the year following their application.
  • Applicants typically have a background in computer science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, physics, or related fields.
  • Candidates from the life sciences are also encouraged to apply if they have a strong computational background and significant programming experience.
  • Working language: English.

Required Documents

Applications for the first BMAI cohort are open from 1 September to 1 December 2026. The PhD programme starts in September 2027. Visit the BMAI website for additional information and apply online.

description:
Scholarship Overview

The Berlin Graduate School of Ancient Studies (BerGSAS) is offering 3 predoc scholarships at Freie Universität Berlin in 2027 in the field of Ancient Studies. Funding is available from 1 March 2027 onwards for up to 6 months. An extension is not possible. You receive a scholarship of EUR 1,000 per month.

Purpose of the Predoc Scholarship

The purpose of the predoc scholarship is to develop a dissertation topic as well as to submit an application to scholarship providers (e.g., Elsa Neumann Scholarship; Gerda Henkel Foundation; Studienstiftung des Deutschen Volkes) within the 6-month funding period. It is expected that your doctoral dissertation will be written at and submitted to the Freie Universität. Predoc scholarship holders who successfully apply for external doctoral funding will be admitted as full members to BerGSAS and participate in the curriculum of a structured doctoral program.

Eligibility Criteria

  • At the beginning of the scholarship, you must be enrolled in either a master's program or a doctoral program at the Freie Universität Berlin.
  • Funding is available to students whose Master's thesis is completed and evaluated by 1 December 2026.
  • You must be planning to conduct and complete your doctorate at the Freie Universität Berlin, within BerGSAS.
  • When submitting your application, please specify who the potential academic supervisor of your doctoral dissertation at the Freie Universität Berlin should be. Please enclose her/his letter of confirmation.

Application Documents

  • A letter of motivation (maximum 1 page, A4)
  • A project outline for a doctoral dissertation (ca. 6,000 characters including spaces). The outline should include a title, state of research, aim/main research question, methods and material/evidence.
  • A letter of confirmation of the potential supervisor of your doctoral dissertation at FU Berlin
  • A curriculum vitae (CV, resume)
  • University transcripts: B.A. and M.A. certificates
  • English language certificate e.g., IELTS or TOEFL: C1 (only if your mother tongue is not German or English)
  • In addition, a letter of recommendation from the supervisor of your MA thesis is required. The reviewer should send the letter directly to bergsas@berliner-antike-kolleg.org.

How to Apply

Please send your application as one single PDF file to bergsas@berliner-antike-kolleg.org. Application documents in German or English, Arial 12pt, 1.5 line.

Application dates

MilestoneDate
Application Deadline00:00 CET on 1 December 2026
Funding Start1 March 2027
Funding DurationUp to 6 months

Official Link

https://www.berliner-antike-kolleg.org/en/bergsas/ausschreibungen/index.html

Contact

Dr Regina Attula, regina.attula@berliner-antike-kolleg.org

Important Notes

  • Partially funded: EUR 1,000/month for up to 6 months.
  • Extension is not possible.
  • The selection committee will not consider incomplete or late applications.
  • Part of the Berlin Graduate School of Ancient Studies (BerGSAS).

Scholarship Overview

The Hamad Bin Khalifa University (HBKU) Scholarship 2027 is a fully-funded opportunity offered to international and Qatari students pursuing Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD degrees at HBKU in Qatar. organization.name: Queen Mary University of London
organization.about: Queen Mary University of London is a public research university and a member of the Russell Group. intro: 3-year funded PhD at Queen Mary University of London on intelligent optimisation and control for future power systems. Home tuition fees and London stipend of £22,618/year. Deadline: 30 Nov 2026.
description:
Research position overview

Future power systems will integrate large numbers of diverse resources, ranging from uncertain renewable generation to flexible, controllable, and data-preserving assets such as data centres, electric vehicles, energy storage, and heat pumps. These resources will be owned and operated by different parties (e.g. consumers, aggregators, and system operators), connected at different voltage levels, and coordinated through a combination of electricity markets (e.g. flexibility), network services (e.g. ancillary services) and local control systems (e.g. active distribution networks).

Optimisation-driven energy management and control are essential to ensure safe and reliable power systems operations while controlling energy resources in the most economical way to improve energy affordability, integrate renewable generation and respond to changing system conditions. However, existing methods, including many machine learning (ML)-enabled methods investigated in smart grid, remain limited in addressing pressing challenges such as maintaining system resilience under unseen and adverse events, reconciling conflicting optimisation objectives, and handling incomplete or privacy-sensitive data. This PhD project aims to address the emerging challenges posed by increasingly decentralised and data-rich power systems, developing novel optimisation and ML-based frameworks that can coordinate heterogeneous resources while maintaining system security, resilience, and economic performance.

Research Objectives

The successful candidate will investigate how distributed energy resources, flexible demand, and emerging cyber-physical infrastructures can be coordinated while respecting physical, computational, and privacy constraints. Research directions may include, but are not limited to:

  • Network-constrained optimisation of distributed energy resources. Develop optimisation and control methods for coordinating distributed energy resources while respecting network constraints and operational requirements. This includes supporting the secure and economical operation of increasingly complex and active distribution networks.
  • Privacy-preserving energy flexibility management. Investigate approaches for coordinating energy flexibility without requiring access to sensitive operational or consumer data.
  • Machine learning-based grid control under adverse conditions. Explore learning-enabled control and decision-making methods for smart grid that can maintain reliable performance under challenging operating conditions.

Your research direction will be shaped by the synergy between your interests and background, which you will refine into a detailed proposal during the first months of the PhD. We welcome candidates with backgrounds in Electrical Power Engineering or Electrical and Electronic Engineering; candidates from Computer Science or Artificial Intelligence who have a strong interest in power systems research are also welcome to apply. Strong programming skills (e.g. Python) and knowledge of machine learning are required. Demonstrated interest in research (e.g. publications) will be an advantage.

Supervisor

Dr Da Huo (he/his) – d.huo@qmul.ac.uk

Funding

The PhD student will receive tuition fees at the home rate and a London stipend at QMUL stipend rates (currently in 2026/27 of £22,618 per year, to be confirmed for subsequent years) annually during the PhD period, which can span for 3 years. Non-home/non-UK students may apply, but if accepted, they will be responsible for the substantial difference in tuition fees, as no additional funding or fee waiver is available to cover this gap.

How to Apply

Applicants should submit their application following the instructions at: http://eecs.qmul.ac.uk/phd/how-to-apply/

The application should include the following:

  • CV (max 2 pages)
  • Cover letter (max 4,500 characters) stating clearly in the first page whether you are eligible for a scholarship as a UK resident
  • Research proposal (max 500 words)
  • 2 References
  • Certificate of English Language (for students whose first language is not English)
  • Other Certificates

intro: Fully funded PhD evaluating novel mineral sources for treatment of micronutrient deficiencies in humans at ETH Zurich. Clinical trials focus. Rolling review.
description:
Project Overview

The ETH Zurich Laboratory of Epigenetics, Nutrition and Metabolism and Sustainable Food Processing Group in the Department of Health Science and Technology are running a joint strategic research line on Microalgae and plant-based foods in Human Nutrition and Health. We are recruiting a talented and highly motivated doctoral student on the topic of 'Novel sources of minerals for treatment of micronutrient deficiencies in humans', focusing on investigating the absorption and bioavailability of novel mineral sources in vivo in clinical trials.

Project Background

Micronutrient deficiency is a widespread global health problem, primarily driven by inadequate dietary intake. More than 5 billion people are estimated to not consume enough of at least one micronutrient. Among those, mineral deficiencies can be particularly critical, namely, iron, calcium, zinc, and magnesium deficiencies, which are particularly common in low- and middle-income countries due to low-mineral diets and primarily affect women and children.

Dietary minerals are typically obtained from a variety of foods including animal-based products such as meat, dairy, and seafood, and plant-based foods such as legumes, cereals, nuts, seeds, and leafy vegetables. However, reliance on conventional animal-based foods raises concerns related to environmental sustainability, ethical considerations, and dietary preferences. Although plant-based foods are generally more sustainable, they often have lower mineral content, bioaccessibility, as well as bioavailability due to the presence of absorption inhibitors such as phytates and polyphenols.

Novel mineral sources, such as microalgae, could be a rich source of essential minerals, including iron, calcium, zinc, and magnesium, along with proteins, lipids, vitamins, and other bioactive compounds. However, the bioavailability of these minerals needs to be assessed with in vivo clinical trials before large scale application in humans.

Job Description

As a doctoral student, you will be responsible for research working towards exploring the absorption and bioavailability of novel mineral sources with clinical trials.

  • Summarize the existing knowledge on minerals from novel sources for human nutrition and health
  • Design intervention meals (including sensory test) for clinical trials
  • Assess the bioaccessibility of minerals in vitro
  • Evaluate the mineral bioavailability in vitro
  • Carry out clinical trials related to human nutrition enriched with novel mineral sources (key)
  • Support teaching activities and co-supervise MSc and BSc students
  • Act at the interface between science and technology when supervising students and collaborating with partners from academia and industry
  • Support grant applications for the team and support related activities from Singapore-ETH Centre, Bezos Centre for Sustainable Protein at NUS, ETH World Food System Center WFSC, and ETH for Development ETH4D competence center

Profile

  • A MSc in Nutrition and Health, Clinical Trials, Food Science and Technology (with strong nutrition or clinical experience), or relevant fields
  • A strong passion for nutrition and health, sustainability, and novel food sources
  • Expertise and interest in working with human/clinical related works (GCP certificate is compulsory, however, can be obtained after starting)
  • Experience and strong interest in nutrition assessment using in vivo models
  • Ability to work in a dynamic, international, and interdisciplinary team
  • Ability to collaborate with different teams and national and international partners
  • Interest in working independently and supervising students
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills in English
  • Scientific curiosity and motivation to perform scientifically rigorous experimental work

We Offer

  • Working with a leading research team on Microalgae and Plant-based Foods in Human Nutrition and Health with strong support from both ETH groups.
  • State-of-the-art research equipment in an excellent and open working environment.
  • Excellent training opportunities for career development and strong networks in both sustainable food and nutrition.
  • The project will also get support from research assistants when needed.
  • Living expenses will be supported with a fixed-rate standard monthly doctoral student salary according to ETH guidelines.

Application Requirements

Submit online application with the following documents (In English, PDF format):

  • Motivation letter (max. 1 page) outlining your qualifications and motivation for this project
  • Research proposal (max. 3 pages) within the project background described above (own designed proposal)
  • CV with contact details of two referees (name, affiliation, position, email address; one referee should be from your current organization)
  • Degree certificates (e.g., Master's and Bachelor's degree) and transcript of records
  • Copies of BSc and MSc theses (any language), if possible and not confidential

If you haven't completed your MSc studies at the time of submission, please substitute the MSc diploma with a written statement by your supervisor specifying the expected completion date.

Applications without these documents will not be considered.

description:
Offer Description

Optical Vortex Generation Using Twisted Bilayer Photonic Crystals.

The Lobet research team part of the NISM institute of the Science Faculty of the University of Namur (Belgium), is looking for a PhD candidate part of a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) doctoral network SPARK project on the topic of "Optical Vortex Generation Using Twisted Bilayer Photonic Crystals" to perform theoretical and numerical calculations, as well as experimental fabrication and characterization in the novel domain of "moiré optics", in collaboration with Prof. M. Piccardo (INESC MN) and Prof. Pol Van Dorpe (IMEC).

Research/Project Description

Moiré photonics is the emerging branch of photonics studying novel platforms made of two photonic crystals disoriented relative to each other, with a tunable rotation angle. They are directly inspired by twistronics, investigating the electronic properties of twisted 2D materials. Driven by the electronic-photonic analogy, twisted structures start appearing in photonics with similar extremely flat bands in their photonic band structure and consequently slow light properties. However, twistoptics is a nascent field, full of fundamental, numerical and technological challenges.

The project will explore the generation of optical vortices carrying orbital angular momentum from twisted photonic crystal structures. The goal is to design twisted photonic crystals to realize robust vortex radiation.

Secondments include 3 months at IMEC for nanofabrication exposure and 6 months at INESC MN (M. Piccardo) for structured-light characterization based on off-axis digital holography. By producing robust vortex beams via twisted photonic platforms, the doctoral candidate contributes to one of the research objectives of the doctoral network SPARK, which is to demonstrate metamaterial-enabled structured light generation through controlled angular momentum.

The SPARK network is coordinated by Humeyra Caglayan (TU/e EE) and brings together Nicolò Maccaferri (UMU), Iñigo Liberal (UPNA), Paloma Arroyo Huidobro (UAM), Marco Piccardo (INESC MN and Técnico Lisboa), Michaël Lobet (UNamur), Riccardo Sapienza (Imperial), and Ahmed H. Dorrah (TU/e AP). It will hire 15 PhD students that will work closely to advance spatiotemporal photonic technologies.

Research Environment

The Michaël Lobet's Research Team at UNamur, part of the NISM institute, has long-standing expertise in theoretical and numerical physics, especially in photonics. The direct work environment is composed of experienced researchers such as Prof. Michaël Lobet, Prof. Luc Henrard, Prof. Olivier Deparis and Prof. Alexandre Mayer. The candidate will benefit from the scientific network of the lab including several high-ranked universities. The lab members have access to state-of-the-art HPC Tier 2 facilities through the CECI consortium and supercomputer facilities of the regional Tier-1 (Zenobe). The PhD will join a dynamic team, composed of 2 post-docs, 5 PhD students and 2 masters.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Master's degree in fields of physics, astrophysics, applied Physics, Optics, Electrical Engineering, Material Engineering or a closely related subject.
  • You should not have a doctoral degree at the time of recruitment.
  • You must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Belgium for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the recruitment (MSCA mobility rule).
  • Strong skills in the English language.
  • Expertise in photonics, numerical methods, and/or scientific computing/HPC or in nanofabrication/optical characterization are strong assets but not a requirement.
  • Team player spirit, willing to collaborate with external institution colleagues, autonomy in work as well as transparency are looked for.

Benefits

  • Gross salary starting around €3,000/month, with potential for additional funding depending on family status (Mobility allowance around €700/month and family allowance around €650/month depending on family status).
  • 36 months funded through the SPARK MSCA network, additional 12 months funded by UNamur to finish the 4 years thesis, with additional benefits for employees.
  • 6-month research stay at INESC MN, Portugal and 3-month research at IMEC, Belgium.
  • Training program including research-specific and transferable skills courses.
  • Active participation in workshops, conferences, and network-wide events.
  • Stimulating, multidisciplinary, and international research environment within a European training network.
  • Starting date foreseen between February 1st 2027 and May 1st 2027.

Application Requirements

  • A curriculum vitae including publications and teaching experiences if any.
  • A list of all master courses with corresponding ECTS and individual scores obtained.
  • A personal letter (1-3 pages) introducing yourself, describing previous research fields and main research results if any, describing personal goals and how you fit in the application.
  • Up to 3 persons of reference that could be contacted to assess the applicant's qualifications.
  • All other information that might be relevant.

The Stagkourakis Lab at Karolinska Institutet and SciLifeLab in Stockholm is recruiting a PhD student in computational neuroscience. Project Overview

The Robotic Materials group at ETH Zurich is looking for a highly motivated PhD student to work on programmable materials that access multiple distinct mechanical states for next-generation robotic matter systems. This 4-year PhD position is fully funded.

Project Background

Modern robots increasingly rely on sophisticated mechanisms, such as modular architectures, reconfigurable linkages, deployable structures, and variable-stiffness components, to adapt their bodies to different tasks and environments. However, such adaptability is often achieved by changing geometry, connectivity, or control strategies, while the underlying material properties remain largely fixed.

This project explores a more fundamental route: robotic matter whose constitutive properties can be programmed on demand. By enabling mechanical modulus, viscoelastic response, and flow behavior to be reconfigured within a single continuous body, we aim to move beyond adaptive hardware architectures towards materials that actively participate in robotic function. The long-term vision is to create robots that can tune their physical embodiment through the programmable properties of matter itself.

Job Description

  • Design, synthesis, and rheological characterization of dynamic covalent polymer composites targeting programmable mechanical state transitions.
  • Development of theoretical understanding and multiphysics simulation of material behavior across mechanical regimes.
  • Fabrication and integration of materials into soft robotic demonstrators showcasing multi-state control under external stimuli.
  • Development of spatial addressability strategies to achieve localized state modulation in a continuous material body.
  • Demonstration of robotic functions (locomotion, grasping, navigation through constrictions) that exploit multi-state material behavior.
  • Supervision of bachelor/master students and participation in teaching.
  • This is a full-time position that starts as soon as possible. Applications are evaluated on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Project Overview

The Sensing, Interaction & Perception Lab invites applications for a fully funded PhD position at ETH Zürich at the intersection of robotics, wearable sensing, signal processing, machine learning, and human-computer interaction.

The goal is to develop neuromotor interfaces for dexterous robot teleoperation using two sensing modalities:

  1. Surface electromyography (sEMG) measured at the wrist or forearm, to decode subtle hand and finger activity, continuous movement, and motor intent in real time.
  2. Egocentric vision as a complementary input channel to provide context about the surrounding scene, manipulated objects, hand–object interactions, and task state.

The PhD will focus on computational and sensing methods required to make such systems robust, generalizable, and effective in real interactive settings, including multimodal learning and reasoning across neuromotor and egocentric visual signals, while exploring applications in Mixed Reality and other interactive systems.

Note: This is not a position in biomedical engineering and there is no health focus.

Project Background

Wearable EMG provides a direct and unobtrusive way to sense muscle activity underlying hand and finger movements. Making such interfaces work reliably outside controlled settings remains a substantial research problem due to variability across users, electrode placement, contact conditions, and noise. This motivates research in signal processing, temporal machine learning, representation learning, adaptation, and real-time inference.

A second challenge is that neuromotor signals alone provide limited information about what the user is interacting with and why a particular movement is occurring. The project will therefore combine EMG with egocentric vision to capture objects, hands, contacts, affordances, and task state. This creates a multimodal research problem: learning representations that combine neuromotor and visual information and developing methods for reasoning about human intent, hand–object interaction, and the state of an ongoing manipulation task.

For robotic teleoperation, these multimodal signals can support systems that jointly reason about what action the user intends, which object or target the action refers to, and how that intent should be translated to a robot with a different embodiment. Relevant problems include dexterous manipulation, shared autonomy, multimodal intent inference, and reasoning over sequences of human and robot actions.

Job Description

  • Develop signal-processing and machine-learning methods for multichannel EMG, including discrete and continuous decoding of hand and finger activity.
  • Develop egocentric computer-vision methods for understanding hands, objects, hand–object interactions, contacts, affordances, and task state.
  • Develop multimodal learning and reasoning methods that combine EMG with egocentric vision to infer motor intent and interaction context.
  • Investigate reasoning over objects, actions, interaction sequences, and task state to resolve ambiguous motor signals and anticipate intended actions.
  • Apply methods to dexterous robot teleoperation, including mapping human motor intent to robot manipulators and dexterous hands.
  • Optionally: Prototype wearable sensing systems, including electrode configurations, signal acquisition, embedded processing, and hardware/software integration (huge plus).
  • Develop and evaluate applications in robotics, Mixed Reality, and other interactive systems.
  • Disseminate findings in publications at top-tier venues and open-source research results and tools where appropriate.
  • Present research findings at academic conferences, workshops, and seminars.

Profile

ETH requirements:

  • Written and spoken fluency in English.
  • An excellent master's degree (MSc., M.Eng. or equivalent) in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or related field.

You bring:

  • A strong foundation in machine learning, including classification and regression, model evaluation, representation learning, and generalization.
  • A solid understanding of signals and time-series data (e.g., sampling, frequency, phase, noise, spectral representations, and filtering).
  • Strong programming skills and experience implementing and quantitatively evaluating computational methods.
  • An interest in building real-time sensing and interactive systems, including experimentation with physical sensors.

A strong background in one or more of the following areas is particularly beneficial:

  • Electrical engineering and signal processing: EMG or other electrophysiological signals, sensor systems, embedded systems, electronics, or wearable sensing.
  • Robotics: manipulation, dexterous manipulation, teleoperation, robot learning, shared autonomy, or human-robot interaction.
  • Computer Vision: egocentric vision, hand and object pose estimation, hand–object interaction, contact and affordance estimation, video understanding, or action recognition.
  • Machine learning: temporal modeling, representation learning, multimodal learning, multimodal reasoning, domain adaptation, or learning from noisy sensor data.
  • Interactive systems: HCI, Mixed Reality, wearable computing, or real-time input systems.

We do not expect applicants to already be experts across all of these areas.

We Offer

  • An exciting research environment and team to study in and work with.
  • Opportunity to develop complete research systems spanning wearable sensing, egocentric perception, machine learning, and robotic interaction.
  • Collaboration with internationally recognized research groups in robotics, machine learning, computer vision, interactive systems, and Mixed Reality.
  • Opportunity to contribute to and collaborate with the ETH AI Center and engage in ETHAR, ETH's Research Hub for Augmented Reality in collaboration with Google XR.
  • Access to infrastructure for wearable and embedded prototyping, egocentric sensing, interactive systems, and robotic manipulation.
  • Support for publication and presentation at leading international conferences and journals.
  • Encouragement of intellectual independence and technically ambitious research.

Application Requirements

Project Overview

Empa, the Swiss Federal Laboratories for Materials Science and Technology, is offering a PhD position in the development of life-like materials that learn, remember, and forget for use in soft robotics. This project is part of an SNSF Ambizione grant led by Dr. Livius F. Muff, hosted in the group of Dr. Luciano Boesel at Empa. The work will primarily be carried out at Empa St. Gallen under the direct supervision of Dr. Livius F. Muff. The PhD student will be affiliated at ETH Zürich (Prof. René Rossi, D-HEST).

The research group designs mechanically robust, multi-responsive polyurethane elastomers with backbone-integrated molecular switches. The aim is to move beyond conventional stimuli-responsive materials toward life-like materials that genuinely learn: forming memories, consolidating them over time, selectively forgetting, and adapting their behavior through experience, all while retaining commercial-grade mechanical properties.

In this PhD project, you will synthesize and characterize semi-crystalline polyurethane elastomers containing backbone-integrated photo-, halo-, and thermochromic molecular switches, and investigate how their interactions can be engineered to produce quantifiable memory and learning behaviors.

Your Tasks

  • Synthesize libraries of single-, dual-, and triple-switch polyurethanes (Stenhouse salt, DASA, and Spiropyran) via copolymerization and post-polymerization functionalization, and validate backbone integration by NMR, GPC, DSC, DMA, tensile testing, UV-Vis spectroscopy, and pump probe characterization.
  • Design and characterize synergistic switching cascades (collaborative, competitive, and interdependent pathways) using time-resolved and spatially resolved spectroscopy, patterned illumination, and pH/thermal stimuli.
  • Develop and validate logic maps for memory formation, consolidation, and selective forgetting, and translate these into training-recall-forgetting cycles on physical polymer films and bilayer actuators.
  • Contribute to integrating learning materials into soft robotic bilayer actuators and, together with the wider team, demonstrate behavioral adaptation in autonomous soft robots.
  • Collaborate with international partners.

Your Profile

  • Strong background in Organic Chemistry, Polymer Chemistry, Materials Science, or a closely related field.
  • Highly motivated, curious person who enjoys working at the interface of synthetic chemistry, materials science, and soft robotics.
  • Comfortable in a multidisciplinary, collaborative environment.

description:
Programme Overview

The EPSRC Centre for Doctoral Training (CDT) in Robotics and AI for Net Zero (RAINZ) is a 4-year fully funded PhD programme across the Universities of Manchester, Glasgow, and Oxford. The programme covers the full lifecycle of Net Zero energy generation assets including wind turbines, solar arrays, and nuclear reactors.

Programme Structure

  • Year 1: Taught MSc at the University of Manchester. Must achieve average of 65% or higher to progress to PhD studies.
  • Years 2-4: PhD research at Manchester, Glasgow, or Oxford, depending on project.
  • Annual residential research sprints where students demonstrate work on industry-defined demonstration rigs.
  • Supported by more than 20 companies from net zero and robotics sectors providing funding, training, secondments, and facilities access.

Partner Research Groups

  • Glasgow: Autonomous Systems and Connectivity division. RAI test environment with multi-robot fleets, self-certification of autonomy systems, and international teleoperation trials.
  • Manchester: Robotics and AI Centre. One of the UK's premier robotics centres with interdisciplinary partnerships.
  • Oxford: Robotics Institute. Expertise in machine learning, AI, computer vision, fabrication, multispectral sensing, perception, and systems engineering.

Funding

  • 4-year studentship covering tuition fees at Home rate.
  • Tax-free stipend at UKRI minimum rate: £21,805 (2026/27 UKRI minimum) for (2026/27 rate applies), rising annually with inflation.
  • TechExpert enhancement: Home applicants receive additional £10,000 per year (approximately £30,780/year total for Home students).
  • Research Training and Support Grant covering travel, consumables, conferences, and secondments.
  • Accessibility fund for students with specific needs.
  • International applicants: Limited studentships (max 30% of cohort per EPSRC rules). Funding fixed at Home fee level. Discuss tuition fee waivers at interview. Visa fees, travel, and IHS not covered.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Undergraduate degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics, or related STEM discipline with at least Upper Second-class (2:1 with 65% average) or international equivalent.
  • Demonstrable programming experience required.
  • Cannot already hold a PhD qualification.
  • Individual projects may have further project-specific requirements.

Application Process

  1. Select a project first. May apply for up to three projects on a single application form. Do not contact supervisory team members directly.
  2. Prepare documents including official university transcripts (undergraduate and postgraduate). Non-English transcripts need authenticated English translations.
  3. Complete the RAINZ CDT application form when applications open.
  4. If progressing, submit formal application through host university portal.
  5. Applications checked against academic entry requirements, reviewed by academic panel, shortlisted candidates invited to online interviews.

Lancaster University, in collaboration with SP Electricity North West (SP ENWL), invites applications for a fully funded PhD studentship. Project Overview

Lancaster University’s School of Engineering, in partnership with United Kingdom National Nuclear Laboratory (UKNNL), invites applications for a fully funded PhD studentship. The project will develop novel data-driven, robust, and adaptive control methods for human–robot interaction and teleoperation, with direct applications in nuclear robotics, hazardous environment manipulation, and beyond.

Project Details

Teleoperation is a critical enabler for safe and efficient operation in hazardous environments such as nuclear decommissioning. Current industrial solutions suffer from limitations under uncertainty, time delays, and noisy sensing. This PhD will design and experimentally validate a hybrid motion–force control framework that ensures precise end-effector positioning while maintaining robust and adaptive force regulation. Research includes development of nonlinear robust adaptive controllers and disturbance observers, design of bilateral teleoperation schemes, integration of data-driven approaches for force estimation, and experimental validation on industrial robotic platforms at the UKNNL Hot Robotics Facility.

  • Coverage: UKRI minimum stipend, tuition fees for Home students, and a research training support grant.
  • Additional support for consumables, maintenance, and travel.

intro: 4-year funded at the Home-fee rate PhD in Bioelectronics and Robotics at UCL. £28,955/year stipend. Open until filled. Apply early.
description:
OpportunityPhD Studentship in Bioelectronics and Robotics at UCL
HostUniversity College London
LocationLondon, United Kingdom
Study LevelPhD
FundingPartially Funded, stipend provided
Stipend£28,955 per year stipend plus Home-rate tuition fees.
Application DeadlineNo closing date - open until suitable candidate found
ApplyOfficial application page ↗

Tuition coverage to check

The advertised package covers Home-rate tuition. It should not be treated as full international-fee funding: confirm your fee status and any overseas-fee difference with the university before accepting.

Project Overview

This is a 4-year, funded at the Home-fee rate PhD studentship in Bioelectronics and Robotics at UCL (University College London), supervised by Dr Yu Wu. The position is based in the Department of Electronic & Electrical Engineering. There is no fixed closing date; applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until a suitable candidate is found.

Research Project

The project combines bioelectronics and robotics to build safer, more adaptive robotic systems for medical and healthcare settings. The aim is to develop sensing-driven control approaches that let robots move with improved safety, precision, and responsiveness when assisting patients or supporting clinical procedures.

You will explore the integration of bioelectronic sensing technologies with robotic platforms, so that robots can detect physiological and environmental signals and translate them into actionable control strategies. The research spans sensing interface development, control algorithm design, and system integration.

Core research tasks include:

  • Design and implementation of bioelectronic sensing systems for robotic platforms.
  • Development of adaptive control algorithms that use real-time physiological and environmental data.
  • Integration and testing of robotic systems for safe interaction with patients and healthcare professionals.

The project sits at the interface of biomedical engineering, soft robotics, and intelligent control systems, in a collaborative environment focused on translating advanced research into practical applications.

Funding Details

The studentship covers 4 years of Home-rate tuition fees plus an annual stipend of £28,955 for living costs. The stipend is paid throughout the studentship.

Key funding facts:

  • The stipend is for living costs and is paid throughout the studentship.
  • International students are welcome to apply but will only receive funding at the Home rate. This means the studentship pays tuition at the Home fee level, and any gap between Home and international fees would need to be covered by the applicant (via external scholarships or personal funding).
  • Full funding details and budget rules are published on UCL's Research Studentship Budgets page.

Qualifications Required

The ideal candidate has a strong academic record in Electronic Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related discipline. Specifically:

  • A strong academic record in Electronic Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • Solid understanding of circuit and system-level design, with experience implementing complex edge devices in resource-constrained environments.
  • Practical experience designing hardware accelerators and versatile programming approaches for data-intensive applications.
  • Genuine interest in applying these skills to develop robotic systems capable of safe and adaptive interaction in healthcare environments.

Eligibility condition: the candidate must pass the entry requirements of the PhD programme at UCL EEE (MPhil/PhD in Electronic and Electrical Engineering).

How to Apply

  1. Submit the application through the UCL online system using the standard UCL postgraduate study application form, and mark it to the attention of Dr Yu Wu.
  2. Prepare a summary of your research interests/proposal (maximum two pages) describing how your background fits the PhD project. New ideas relevant to the research field are explicitly welcome.
  3. For informal enquiries, email Dr Yu Wu directly (yu.wu.09@ucl.ac.uk). She is happy to answer any questions about the project before you apply.

Practical advice on timing: since the advert states there is no closing date and the position remains open only until a suitable candidate is found, this is effectively a rolling recruitment. Strong applicants are reviewed as they apply, and earlier applications stand a better chance.

Equality, Diversity & Inclusion

UCL actively encourages applications from underrepresented backgrounds in engineering, including women, ethnic minorities, and people with disabilities. The department states that its research is driven by researchers and PhD students from countries and backgrounds across the globe.

About UCL and the Department

UCL is London's leading multidisciplinary university, founded in 1826, with more than 11,000 staff and 38,000 students from 150 different countries. It was the first university in England to welcome students of any religion and the first to admit women on equal terms.

The Department of Electronic & Electrical Engineering is the UK's first EEE department, founded in 1885 by Sir John Ambrose Fleming FRS. In the 2014 Research Excellence Framework, it was ranked the leading EEE department in the UK for research outputs.

The CVISS Lab (Computer Vision for Smart Structure Laboratory) and iNDT Laboratory at the University of Waterloo, Canada, are recruiting graduate researchers and postdocs for condition and safety assessment of infrastructure using non-destructive testing (NDT) combined with computer vision and AI.

intro: Fully funded scholarship at MBZUAI Abu Dhabi. Automatic full scholarship for all admitted graduate students (M.Sc./Ph.D.): 100% tuition waiver, monthly stipend, accommodation, health insurance. Deadline: 15 Dec 2026.

Programme Overview

The MBZUAI Scholarship 2027 at the Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI) in Abu Dhabi is automatically granted to every admitted full-time student. There is no separate scholarship form. The scholarship provides 100% tuition waiver, monthly stipend, on-campus accommodation, health insurance, and UAE visa sponsorship. The 2027 application portal opens 7 September 2026 and closes 15 December 2026 at 5:00 PM GST.

Scholarship Model

MBZUAI operates a distinctive funding structure: admission equals funding. Every student admitted to a full-time eligible GRADUATE program (M.Sc./Ph.D.; the Master in Applied AI (MAAI) is excluded) receives the full scholarship package automatically. Undergraduate applicants are considered for separate merit-based and need-based scholarships covering up to 100% of tuition and cost of attendance. There is no separate scholarship application, essays, or selection rounds. The admission itself is the competition.

Financial Coverage

  • 100% tuition fee waiver for the full program duration.
  • Monthly stipend: International MSc students receive AED 15,500 gross/month (approximately AED 8,000 net take-home with housing deducted); International PhD students receive AED 17,500 gross/month (approximately AED 10,000 net take-home). Married PhD students receive additional AED 5,000/month housing allowance. UAE nationals receive significantly higher stipends: AED 37,500/month (MSc) and AED 43,500/month (PhD).
  • On-campus student accommodation in Masdar City campus.
  • Health insurance and UAE visa/residence sponsorship for non-UAE nationals.
  • Annual return airfare to home country for funded international students.
  • Dedicated faculty supervision from internationally renowned AI researchers.

Programs Available for 2027 Intake

  • Master's and PhD: Machine Learning, Computer Vision, Natural Language Processing, Robotics, Statistics and Data Science, Computational Biology.
  • Undergraduate: Bachelor of Science in Artificial Intelligence (Engineering or Business stream).

Eligibility Criteria

  • Bachelor's degree in a STEM field from a university accredited or recognized by UAE Ministry of Education.
  • Minimum CGPA of 3.0-3.5/4.0 depending on program (MSc programs typically list 3.2 minimum).
  • English proficiency: IELTS Academic minimum 6.5, TOEFL iBT minimum 90, PTE Academic 60, or Cambridge C1.
  • Statement of purpose required.
  • Research proposal required only for PhD applicants.
  • GRE optional, not mandatory.
  • Two recommendation letters typically required.
  • CV/resume highlighting research, projects, and technical skills. GitHub/technical portfolio recommended.

intro: The Rotary Yoneyama Scholarship 2027 for Overseas Candidates at Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific University (APU) provides ¥140,000 per month for two years to Master's and PhD students plus up to ¥250,000 in travel reimbursement. Foundation application window: 1-31 October 2026. APU deadlines: 15 September 2026 (Sept 2027 intake) and 7 October 2026 (April 2027 intake). This award provides living-cost support; tuition fees are not covered.
description:
Programme Overview

The Rotary Yoneyama Scholarship 2027 for Overseas Candidates at Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific University (APU) is run by Japan's largest private scholarship foundation. It provides ¥140,000 per month for two years to Master's and PhD students plus up to ¥250,000 in travel reimbursement. This is a living-cost scholarship, not a tuition award.

Application dates

MilestoneDate
APU application deadline — September 2027 intake15 September 2026
Foundation application portal opens1 October 2026, 13:00 JST
APU application deadline — April 2027 intake7 October 2026
Foundation application portal closes31 October 2026, 13:00 JST
Selection results by emailMid-March 2027
Certificate of eligibility issuedEnd of March 2027
Stipend payments beginApril 2027 (April intake) / Sept–Oct 2027 (fall intake)

Financial Coverage

  • ¥140,000 monthly stipend for two years (Master's and Doctoral students).
  • Travel subsidy up to ¥250,000 toward economy airfare and related costs, reimbursed after arrival in Japan.
  • Host-club network and cultural exchange: each scholar assigned to a local Rotary Sewa Club and personal counselor.

Not Covered

  • Tuition and admission fees. APU charges a ¥200,000 admission fee plus tuition of roughly ¥1,655,000 in the first year of the Master's program (approximately ¥3,110,000 across two years).
  • Remedy: APU's own Tuition Reduction Scholarship (30%, 50%, 65%, 80%, or 100%) applied within the APU admission application.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Must not hold Japanese nationality, including dual nationals.
  • Must be able to obtain a student visa for study in Japan.
  • Must be residing outside Japan until the program begins.
  • Must not have resided in Japan for more than 31 days in total (exceptions apply for family situations or Rotary Youth Exchange).
  • JLPT N3 or above must be passed at the time of application.
  • Born after 2 April 1982 (under 45 years old at award).
  • Not a past recipient of a Yoneyama scholarship.
  • Not concurrently holding another major living-cost scholarship such as MEXT or JDS.
  • Research (non-degree) students are not eligible.

Eligible APU Graduate Programs

  • Master's Program in Asia Pacific Studies (APS)
  • Master's Program in International Cooperation Policy (ICP)
  • Doctoral Program in Asia Pacific Studies
  • MBA program (Graduate School of Management)

All graduate classes at APU are conducted in English.

Application Process (Dual-Track)

  1. Apply directly to the Foundation through its web portal (around March for April enrollment or August for September enrollment).
  2. Apply to APU and mark the Rotary Yoneyama Scholarship candidacy box in the APU Online Application System by 15 September 2026 (Sept 2027 intake) or 7 October 2026 (April 2027 intake).
  3. Receive the Letter of Acceptance from APU after admission results are announced.
  4. Submit the Acceptance Letter to the Foundation to complete the scholarship file.
  5. Selection results emailed by mid-March 2027. If rejected for university admission, scholarship eligibility is lost.

Required Documents (Foundation)

  • Application for Scholarship (official form)
  • Research Plan at Japanese University
  • Essay: Why I chose to study in Japan. My future plan after studying in Japan.
  • Recommendation Letter from supervisor/professor of targeted graduate school
  • Copy of admission application submitted to APU
  • Academic transcripts and degree documentation
  • JLPT certificate (N3 or above)

Scholar Obligations (Sewa Club System)

  • Assigned to a host Rotary club and personal counselor.
  • Communicate in Japanese at club meetings.
  • Attend host club's regular monthly meetings.
  • Give speeches and participate in Rotary District activities.
  • Submit activity report twice a year (September and February).
  • Maintain alumni relationship after scholarship ends.

Official Links

  • Rotary Yoneyama Memorial Foundation: https://www.rotary-yoneyama.or.jp/english/overseas
  • APU Rotary Yoneyama Scholarship instructions: https://admissions.apu.ac.jp/graduate/how_to_apply/external_scholarship/rotary_yoneyama
  • APU Graduate admissions: https://admissions.apu.ac.jp/graduate
  • APU Graduate tuition fees: https://en.apu.ac.jp

Important Notes

  • Fully Funded label is misleading: stipend and travel allowance cover living costs only; tuition must be met through APU Tuition Reduction Scholarship or other funds.
  • The 7 October deadline is APU-side for April 2027 intake; September 2027 intake closes 15 September 2026. Foundation window runs full month of October 2026.
  • JLPT N3+ at application is mandatory. Host-club obligations are formal award conditions.

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the deadline: 31 October 2026, 13:00 JST. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.

Scholarship Overview

The Doha Institute for Graduate Studies (DI) is accepting applications for its fully funded Master's and PhD scholarships for the 2027–2028 academic year. The application window runs from 1 September 2026 to 15 January 2027. These scholarships are open to all nationalities and provide comprehensive financial support.

Scholarship Types

  1. Tamim Scholarship (Merit-Based)
  • For academically outstanding students admitted to Master's programs.
  • International students receive: 100% tuition waiver, free accommodation in institute dormitories, monthly stipend, health insurance, and two round-trip airfare tickets (one on arrival, one after graduation).
  • Qatari nationals without external sponsorship receive a full tuition waiver.
  1. Sanad Scholarship (Need-Based)
  • For Qatari citizens, residents, and international students with demonstrated financial need.
  • Tuition coverage ranges from 10% to 100% based on need.
  • International students receiving Sanad are also eligible for full tuition, free accommodation, monthly stipend, and health insurance.
  1. Doctoral Scholarships (Three Phases)
  • Funding is released in stages tied to academic milestones.
  • Recipients must work for the Institute at least 10 hours per week (partial grantees up to 15 hours).
  • Phase 1: Covers two semesters of first-phase coursework.
  • Phase 2: Covers one academic year for full-time prospectus reading; requires GPA of at least 3.5 in first-phase courses.
  • Phase 3: Covers two academic years for dissertation writing, unlocked after passing the comprehensive examination.

---

Financial Coverage & Living Allowances

Winning a scholarship here means stepping into a worry-free life where your basic needs are already taken care of.

Monthly Stipend – A reliable monthly allowance covers your daily expenses—groceries, transport, and personal essentials—so you can focus entirely on your studies without financial stress.

Free On-Campus Housing – You receive a fully furnished room on campus, free of charge. It places you at the heart of a vibrant academic community, saving you from the hassle and high cost of Doha's rental market.

Health Insurance – Comprehensive medical coverage is provided for the entire program, giving you access to Qatar's top-tier hospitals without any out-of-pocket expenses.

Round-Trip Airfare – The Institute includes two economy-class tickets for international students: one to bring you to Doha, and another to take you home after graduation.

For Doctoral Candidates – PhD funding is structured in phases but remains strong throughout, with teaching and research assistantships that help you grow professionally while you earn.

---

Eligibility Criteria

  • Academic Background:
  • Master's applicants: full-time Bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field. Final-year undergraduates may apply with current transcripts.
  • Doctoral applicants: Bachelor's and Master's degrees. Minimum GPAs typically 3.2/4.0 (Bachelor's) and 3.5/4.0 (Master's).
  • No age restrictions; applicants of any nationality may apply.
  • Language Requirements:
  • Instruction primarily in Arabic. Non-native Arabic speakers take an Arabic proficiency test (oral and written) before admission.
  • English proficiency: IELTS Academic (minimum 5.5), TOEFL iBT 59, or DELF B2 (score 50). Higher English scores may be required for graduation.
  • IELTS waiver: Applicants are exempt if their Bachelor's degree was earned at a university in the US, UK, Canada, Australia, or another institution where English is the official language of instruction. Official documentation must be uploaded.

Available Programs

School of Social Sciences and Humanities (SOSH) – Master's:

  • Clinical Psychology
  • Comparative Literature
  • Conflict Management and Humanitarian Action
  • Critical Security Studies
  • History
  • Human Rights
  • Journalism
  • Linguistics and Arabic Lexicography
  • Media Studies
  • Philosophy
  • Politics and International Relations
  • Social Psychology
  • Social Work
  • Sociology and Anthropology

School of Economics, Administration and Public Policy (SEAPP) – Master's:

  • Public Policy
  • Development Economics
  • Public Administration
  • Executive Master of Public Administration

Doctoral Programs (8):

  • Public Administration
  • Development Economics
  • Politics and International Relations
  • Critical Security Studies
  • Media Studies
  • Sociology
  • History
  • Linguistics and Arabic Lexicography

Several programs hold additional international accreditation from bodies such as FIBAA and NASPAA.

Application Process

  1. Choose a program and confirm specific admission criteria on the official Academic Programs page.
  2. Create an account on the DI admission portal (admissions.dohainstitute.edu.qa). Only one application per applicant is allowed.
  3. Complete the online form; you can save progress and return later.
  4. Upload all required documents directly to the portal.
  5. Request reference letters online; referees receive the request automatically and submit their forms online.
  6. Submit by 15 January 2027.
  7. Shortlisted applicants may be invited for interviews or written exams.
  8. After admission decisions, eligible students are contacted to complete the scholarship application (Tamim for merit, Sanad for need). Doctoral applicants receive the scholarship form directly from the Admissions Office.
  9. Submit the scholarship form with supporting documentation and await the award announcement.

Required Documents

Master's Applicants:

  • Passport copy (international) or Qatari ID (citizens/residents)
  • Certified Bachelor's degree certificate
  • Certified undergraduate transcripts (in Arabic or English), including transferred courses
  • Updated CV/resume
  • Two academic letters of recommendation (submitted online by referees)
  • Personal statement
  • Academic essay (only for SOSH applicants)
  • English test score OR official statement that the degree was taught in English

PhD Applicants (additional):

  • Certified Master's degree and transcripts
  • Copy of Master's thesis, capstone project, or research sample
  • Statement of interest
  • Preliminary doctoral dissertation proposal
  • Three academic reference letters (submitted online)

Official Contact

  • Admissions email: admissions@dohainstitute.edu.qa
  • Scholarships page: https://www.dohainstitute.edu.qa/en/Admissions-Office/Pages/Scholarships.aspx

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the stated deadline. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.

  • Start Date: October 2026
  • Funding Type: Fully Funded (EPSRC)
  • Location: Edinburgh

Project Overview & Significance

The EPSRC Centre for Doctoral Training in Green Industrial Futures (CDT-GIF), led by Heriot-Watt University, is a transformative 4-year PhD programme dedicated to solving the global climate crisis through industrial decarbonisation. As the world transitions towards net-zero emissions, heavy industry faces immense pressure to reduce its carbon footprint. This CDT focuses on the interdisciplinary, whole-systems research required to achieve this green industrial revolution. It brings together engineering, chemistry, and environmental science to develop new technologies and processes that can decarbonise energy-intensive sectors, such as chemicals, materials, and manufacturing. The research aims to provide the scientific and engineering foundations for a sustainable, low-carbon industrial economy.

Research Themes & Objectives

The CDT-GIF encompasses a wide range of research themes, including carbon capture and storage (CCS), hydrogen as a clean fuel, electrification of industrial processes, and circular economy models. The programme emphasises a 'whole-systems' approach, meaning it considers not just the technical feasibility of new technologies, but also their economic, environmental, and social implications. The objective is to train doctoral researchers who can think across disciplines to design and implement industrial systems that are both sustainable and economically viable. Projects often involve close collaboration with industry partners, ensuring the research is directly applicable to real-world decarbonisation challenges.

Training & Development

Students in the CDT-GIF benefit from a structured 4-year programme that includes a foundational first year of taught courses, covering core concepts in industrial decarbonisation and research methods. The cohort-based model fosters a collaborative environment. Training includes access to state-of-the-art laboratories, industry placements, and opportunities to present at international conferences. Graduates emerge with a unique skill set that bridges engineering and sustainability, making them highly sought after by the energy sector, manufacturing industries, and government policy bodies.

Eligibility & Requirements

Applicants must hold a first-class or upper second-class honours degree in engineering, chemistry, physics, or a related discipline. A Master's degree is desirable. The programme is fully funded by EPSRC, with specific eligibility rules regarding nationality and residency. Candidates should demonstrate a strong commitment to sustainability and decarbonisation.

How to Apply & Official Contacts

Cohort 3 project details are currently available for recruitment. Prospective applicants should visit the official CDT-GIF website for specific project details and application instructions. General postgraduate enquiries can be sent to study@hw.ac.uk.

This programme invites researchers to take a holistic view of carbon management, examining the entire life cycle of buildings and infrastructure—from the initial design concept through to demolition and material reuse. Project Overview & Significance

This is a rare opportunity to engage in fundamental wave physics research funded by the European Research Council (ERC) under the ATLANTIS project. Hosted by the Department of Physics and Engineering at King's College London, this project pushes the boundaries of conventional physics. It challenges the standard textbook assumptions about near-field waves. Near-field physics is crucial for advancements in metamaterials, advanced sensing, and high-resolution imaging. By removing traditional assumptions, the research aims to uncover new physical phenomena and methodologies that could revolutionise how we manipulate and understand wave-matter interactions at the nanoscale.

Research Themes & Objectives

The successful candidates will investigate the fundamental limits and behaviours of near-field waves in complex media. The research will likely involve theoretical modelling, computational simulations, and potentially experimental validation. Key areas of interest include the engineering of metamaterials with exotic properties, the development of super-resolution sensing technologies, and novel imaging techniques that surpass the diffraction limit. The project is inherently fundamental, meaning it seeks to answer deep physical questions that have broad downstream applications in telecommunications, medical imaging, and materials science.

Training & Development

Funded by the ERC ATLANTIS project, these PhD positions come with exceptional financial support that goes far beyond a standard stipend. Students will have dedicated funding for conference and workshop attendance, allowing them to present their findings to the international scientific community. Additional funding covers training activities, international collaboration and dissemination visits, publication costs in high-impact journals, and access to specialised research software. Candidates will be trained in advanced computational techniques, theoretical physics, and research methodologies, positioning them for leading roles in academia or high-tech industries.

Eligibility & Requirements

Applicants must hold a minimum of an undergraduate degree with a 2:1 honours in physics, engineering, or a closely related subject. A strong background in electromagnetism, wave theory, or computational physics is highly desirable. Given the fundamental nature of the research, candidates should demonstrate a deep curiosity, strong analytical skills, and the ability to tackle complex, abstract problems.

How to Apply

  • Disciplines: Aerospace Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Built Environment, Civil Engineering, Computational Mathematics, Computational Physics, Data Science, Environmental Engineering, Fluid Mechanics, Mechanical Engineering

Research position overview

This PhD project will investigate fast computational approaches for modelling urban airflow and environmental hazard assessment in complex city environments. The research is motivated by emerging challenges in Urban Air Mobility (UAM), UAV operations, emergency response planning, and sustainable urban infrastructure.

The Problem

Urban wind flow strongly influences pollutant dispersion, pedestrian safety, and UAV operation within cities. However, high-fidelity Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations are computationally expensive and generate very large datasets, limiting their use in real-time applications and decision-making.

Research Focus

This project will explore accelerated and reduced-order modelling approaches for urban airflow simulation, potentially including:

  • Lattice Boltzmann Methods (LBM)
  • GPU-accelerated CFD
  • Surrogate modelling
  • Real-time data reduction techniques

Key Research Objectives

The research will focus on converting large volumes of time-dependent CFD outputs into actionable information, such as hazard maps, flow indicators, and environmental risk metrics, without requiring large-scale data storage.

Skills You Will Develop

  • Computational fluid dynamics
  • Scientific programming
  • High-performance computing (HPC)
  • Data processing
  • Urban environmental modelling

Collaboration Opportunities

Depending on the student's interests and project evolution, there may also be opportunities to collaborate with researchers in AI, uncertainty quantification, urban systems, and environmental acoustics.

Supervisor Profile: Dr Marta Camps Santasmasas

Dr Marta Camps Santasmasas is a Lecturer in Aeronautical Engineering at the University of Salford. She develops computer simulations that help us understand how air moves through cities and around structures, supporting applications from wind energy to urban safety.

Research Specialisms

  • Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD)
  • Advanced simulation methods for airflow around structures
  • Atmospheric boundary layer flows (urban wind flow, wind energy)
  • Real time and interactive computational fluid dynamics (CFD)

Professional Background

She is a member of the Women in High Performance Computing network. She previously worked as a research engineer for Normawind, using CFD modelling to optimise wind turbine generators layouts in complex terrains, and as an urban atmospheric modeller for CHAM, an industrial CFD consultancy. She completed her PhD in Computational Fluid Dynamics (2016-2021).

Eligibility Requirements

  • Degree Classification: First Class or 2:1 Honours degree (or equivalent)

Funding Details

Basic Information

  • Host Institution: Various Japanese Universities (NAIST, Osaka University, etc.)
  • Study Level: Master's, PhD
  • Funding Type: Fully Funded (MEXT)
  • Intake: October 2026
  • Stipend (Master's): 144,000 yen/month
  • Stipend (Doctoral): 145,000 yen/month
  • Duration (Master's): October 2026 – September 2028
  • Duration (Doctoral): October 2026 – September 2029
  • Coverage: Full tuition, monthly stipend, travel, health insurance

Project Overview & Significance

The MEXT (Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology) Scholarship is the most scholarship programme offered by the Japanese Government. The 'University Recommendation' pathway allows leading Japanese universities to directly recommend exceptional international candidates for the scholarship. This fully funded programme covers all expenses, ensuring that scholars can focus entirely on their academic and research pursuits. Japan is a global leader in technology, engineering, and scientific research. The MEXT scholarship aims to foster global leaders who will contribute to the academic and industrial collaboration between Japan and the rest of the world. The programme offers an unparalleled cultural and academic experience, allowing students to study in state-of-the-art laboratories while immersing themselves in Japan's rich, traditional culture.

Research Themes & Objectives

The scholarship is open to virtually all academic disciplines, though the participating universities often focus on STEM fields. Participating universities include NAIST, Yokohama National University, Osaka University, Nagoya Institute of Technology, and Tokyo Metropolitan University. Research themes vary widely depending on the chosen university and supervisor, ranging from advanced materials science and artificial intelligence to civil engineering and public policy. The core objective is to facilitate advanced, research while building a global network of Japan-sympathetic leaders and scholars.

Training & Development

MEXT scholars receive comprehensive support, including full tuition coverage, a generous monthly stipend, round-trip airfare, and health insurance. Many universities also offer supplementary Japanese language courses, helping international students integrate into the academic and social environment. Scholars have access to research facilities and are mentored by leading Japanese academics. The programme also includes cultural excursions and networking events, ensuring a well-rounded international experience.

Eligibility & Requirements

Applicants must be citizens of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan. They must hold a Bachelor's degree (for Master's application) or a Master's degree (for PhD application). Academic excellence is the primary criterion. The specific application process and deadlines vary depending on the recommending university, but typically require a strong academic record, letters of recommendation, and a detailed research plan.

How to Apply & Official Contacts

Prospective candidates must first apply directly to the participating Japanese university of their choice. The university's academic committee will review the application and, if successful, recommend the candidate to MEXT. Applicants should monitor the official websites of their target universities for specific application guidelines and deadlines.

Heriot-Watt University's Dubai Campus offers a dynamic, self-funded PhD programme in Computer Sciences, situated in one of the world's fastest-growing technology hubs. This programme provides a unique opportunity to conduct high-impact research in Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, or Cyber Security within a global academic framework. Students will benefit from the university's international reputation and the local ecosystem of tech startups, corporate hubs, and government innovation initiatives. The research produced here aims to solve complex, real-world problems, from securing critical infrastructure to developing AI-driven analytics for smart cities.

The programme covers three primary research areas. 'Data Science' focuses on predictive analytics, big data processing, semantic technologies, and advanced visualisation. 'Cyber Security' involves malware detection, network intrusion prevention, and digital forensics. The objective is to develop algorithms and systems that push the boundaries of current technology. Students at the Dubai Campus have access to modern research facilities and a diverse, international academic community. Project Overview & Significance

King's College London is leading CDTnet, a groundbreaking new European doctoral network that will revolutionise cardiovascular care. The network will support the training of 15 PhD researchers in the development of cardiovascular Digital Twins. A Digital Twin is a highly sophisticated, personalised virtual representation of an individual patient's heart. By simulating the physical and physiological processes of the heart, these digital twins can help detect and assess risks earlier, improve diagnostic accuracy, and support the selection of the most effective, personalised treatment strategies. This project sits at the absolute forefront of computational medicine, bringing together leading universities, clinical institutions, and industry partners across Europe.

Research Themes & Objectives

The research within CDTnet is highly interdisciplinary, combining advanced computational modelling, fluid dynamics, and artificial intelligence to create accurate, predictive cardiac models. The objective is to move beyond generic treatments and enable truly personalised cardiology. By creating a digital twin of a patient's heart, clinicians can test the efficacy of different interventions in a virtual environment before applying them in the real world. This minimises risk and maximises the chances of successful patient outcomes.

Training & Development

As an MSCA-style doctoral network, CDTnet offers an exceptional, structured training programme. PhD researchers will receive comprehensive training in scientific communication, ensuring they can present complex computational concepts to diverse audiences. The programme also includes modules on entrepreneurship, clinical translation, ethics, and leadership. Furthermore, students will receive specialised training in artificial intelligence and innovation, equipping them with the skills needed to bring computational medical technologies from the lab to the clinic. The networked nature of the programme means students will undertake secondments at partner institutions, gaining diverse academic and industry experiences.

Eligibility & Requirements

The network is open to all nationalities. Specific requirements will vary depending on the individual project advertised within the network. Generally, candidates should have a strong background in computer science, physics, biomedical engineering, or medicine, with a keen interest in applying computational methods to cardiology.

How to Apply

Projects will begin being advertised from September 2026 onward. Prospective applicants are advised to monitor the CDTnet website (https://www.cdtnet.eu/) and follow the network on LinkedIn for the latest project adverts and application instructions.

MSCA 2026 rates: doctoral candidates receive a living allowance of €4,010 per month plus a mobility allowance of €710 per month (€660 family top-up where eligible), adjusted by the national correction coefficient.

  • Stipend (PhD): €1,400/month
