  • Fields: All academic disciplines
  • Start: Usually 1 October 2026

Project Overview & Significance

The German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) is the world's largest funding organisation for the international exchange of students and researchers. Its fully funded scholarship programme is a cornerstone of Germany's effort to attract top global academic talent. The DAAD offers scholarships for a wide range of postgraduate courses, including Master's degrees and PhDs, at German higher education institutions. Germany is a global powerhouse in engineering, basic science, and the humanities. The DAAD scholarship aims to foster cross-cultural academic exchange and provide international students with access to Germany's , tuition-free higher education system. The scholarship covers living expenses, travel, and health insurance, ensuring that financial constraints do not hinder brilliant minds from pursuing advanced research in Germany. By supporting scholars across all disciplines, the DAAD promotes a diverse, interdisciplinary academic community.

Research Themes & Objectives

The DAAD supports research across all academic disciplines. Specific programmes often target fields relevant to the sustainable development of the scholars' home countries, such as environmental engineering, public health, or economic policy. However, purely academic or fundamental research in the sciences and humanities is equally supported. The objective is to provide scholars with the highest quality academic training, enabling them to become leaders and innovators who contribute to the academic and economic development of their home regions, while also strengthening Germany's international academic partnerships.

Training & Development

DAAD scholars benefit from more than just financial support; they join a massive, highly active global alumni network. The programme includes a mandatory German language course, helping scholars integrate into the local culture and academic environment. Scholars have access to the facilities of German universities and research institutes like the Max Planck Society and Fraunhofer Society. Training also encompasses intercultural skills and professional development, preparing graduates for global careers.

Eligibility & Requirements

Applicants must hold a Bachelor's degree (for Master's) or a Master's degree (for PhD). They must demonstrate academic excellence. Specific language requirements vary by programme, but proficiency in English or German is usually required. The DAAD particularly encourages applications from developing countries and regions experiencing academic brain drain.

How to Apply & Official Contacts

Applications are typically submitted via the DAAD online portal. Candidates must choose a specific Master's or PhD programme at a German university before applying. The application requires a CV, academic transcripts, a research proposal (for PhD), and letters of recommendation. Deadlines vary by programme but are often a year in advance of the intended start date.

Project Overview & Significance

This self-funded PhD programme in Construction Management and Innovation is designed for professionals and scholars aiming to lead the future of the construction industry. The industry is undergoing rapid transformation, driven by digitalisation, sustainability demands, and the need for greater efficiency. This programme provides a platform to research innovative solutions to these challenges. By examining the whole construction lifecycle, from procurement to project handover, candidates can develop new frameworks for managing complex construction projects. The research aims to improve productivity, reduce costs, and enhance the sustainability of the built environment. Heriot-Watt’s strong industry links ensure that research is grounded in real-world relevance, bridging the gap between academic theory and industrial practice.

Research Themes & Objectives

The programme encompasses several key research areas. 'Construction Project Management' focuses on risk, logistics, and stakeholder management. 'ICT in Construction' explores the application of Building Information Modelling (BIM), digital twins, and smart construction technologies. 'People and Organisation' examines labour dynamics, safety, and organisational behaviour. 'Procurement' researches sustainable supply chains and contract models. Finally, 'Sustainability' integrates green building practices and lifecycle assessment. The objective is to produce research that directly informs industry standards and government policy, fostering a more efficient and sustainable construction sector.

Training & Development

Students will develop advanced skills in research methodology, data analysis, and project management. The programme offers opportunities to engage with industry partners through seminars and site visits. The Edinburgh Campus provides a collaborative environment, with access to the latest software and research databases. Graduates will be well-positioned for senior management roles in construction firms, consultancies, and regulatory bodies.

Eligibility & Requirements

Applicants must hold a first-class or upper second-class honours degree and a Master's degree in construction, civil engineering, or a related field. Relevant industry experience is highly valued. As this is a self-funded programme, applicants must secure their own funding for tuition and living expenses. Both full-time and part-time study options are available.

Project Overview & Significance

The Robotics and Autonomous Systems PhD programme is a , fully funded joint initiative between Heriot-Watt University and the University of Edinburgh, hosted by the Edinburgh Centre for Robotics (ECR). This 4-year programme is at the absolute forefront of global robotics research. It includes the CDT-D2AIR (UKRI AI Centre for Doctoral Training in Dependable and Deployable AI for Robotics) and the EPSRC CDT in Robotics and Autonomous Systems. The programme focuses on developing AI and robotic systems that are not only intelligent but also safe, reliable, and deployable in real-world environments. By bridging the gap between laboratory prototypes and robust, field-deployed robots, the research aims to revolutionise sectors such as healthcare, offshore energy, and manufacturing. Students get access to facilities, including the Robotarium, a state-of-the-art testing arena.

Research Themes & Objectives

The research covers a broad spectrum of robotics, including computer vision, machine learning, control systems, human-robot interaction, and autonomous navigation. The CDT-D2AIR programme specifically emphasises 'dependable' AI, ensuring that algorithms are transparent, fair, and robust. The objective is to train a new generation of roboticists who can design systems capable of operating safely and effectively in complex, dynamic environments. Projects often involve industrial partners, ensuring the research has a direct pathway to commercial and societal impact.

Training & Development

The 4-year programme includes a foundational first year of intensive training, covering both technical robotics skills and broader professional development. Students benefit from cohort-based learning, fostering collaboration across disciplines. The ECR provides access to hardware and software. Throughout the programme, students undertake placements with industry or international academic partners, ensuring they graduate with both a deep theoretical understanding and practical, deployment-focused experience. Graduates are highly sought after by leading tech companies, research institutes, and government agencies.

Eligibility & Requirements

Applicants must hold a first-class or upper second-class honours degree in engineering, computer science, physics, or a related discipline. The programme is highly competitive. Funding is provided by EPSRC and UKRI, with specific eligibility rules regarding nationality and residency. Applicants should demonstrate a strong interest in AI and physical robotics.

The Francis Crick Institute in London is recruiting doctoral candidates for its 2027 PhD programme. The Crick is one of the largest biomedical research institutes in Europe, and its students work alongside research groups spanning cancer, immunology, neuroscience, infection, and the physics and chemistry of living systems. Rather than choosing a single project in isolation, students join a four-year programme that starts with rotations and taught elements before settling into the thesis lab.

Every PhD student at the Crick registers with one of its partner universities, so the final degree comes from a UK institution while the day-to-day research happens inside the Crick's labs on Midland Road, next to St Pancras station. The institute currently hosts more than 200 PhD students and doctoral clinical fellows, and around 60% of them come from the EU and further afield, which makes this one of the more international biomedical PhD environments in the UK.

The Natural History Museum at the University of Oslo is hiring a PhD Research Fellow to work on the diversity and ecology of marine algae and their protistan parasites. title: PhD Positions in Diffractive Electron Imaging of Surfaces at TU Delft, Netherlands
description:
Project Overview

TU Delft is looking for two PhD candidates to join the Curious Beams Lab and develop a new approach to imaging material surfaces with electrons. The positions are part of BEAMSurf: Diffractive Atomic-Scale Surface Imaging with Backscattered Electrons, an ERC Starting Grant project led by Dr. Georgios Varnavides.

Surfaces control many properties and processes that determine material functionality, from chemical reactions in catalysis to interfaces in nanoelectronic devices. BEAMSurf will develop a new scanning electron microscope that uses coherent backscattered electrons for diffractive imaging of surfaces, with the potential to overcome conventional resolution limits for low-energy SEM.

The Two PhD Roles

  • PhD 1 - Electron Optics and Experimental Imaging: design, characterise and integrate miniature electron-optical components into a high-vacuum SEM, separating the backscattered-electron signal from the primary beam.
  • PhD 2 - Computational Imaging and Surface Science: develop forward models and inverse-scattering approaches for reflection-mode electron imaging, moving beyond static images towards surfaces as they evolve.

Research Environment

The Curious Beams Lab is part of the Microscopy and Instrumentation Techniques (MInT) cluster of the Department of Imaging Physics at TU Delft, Faculty of Applied Sciences. The cluster works across electron microscopy, from semiconductor inspection to cryogenic electron microscopy, with access to state-of-the-art field-emission SEMs and FIB-SEMs, including a new microscope acquired for this project.

Additional pay8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% end-of-year bonus.
DurationFour years in principle, split into two contracts: an initial 18-month contract with a go/no-go assessment, followed by 30 months after a satisfactory assessment.
Project fundingERC Starting Grant (BEAMSurf); the team also includes a postdoctoral researcher leading instrumentation development.

Academic preparationMSc or equivalent in physics, applied physics, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, materials science, computer science, or a closely related field.
InterestStrong interest in experimental physics, electron microscopy, imaging science or a related area.
Electron-optics trackExperience or interest in electron optics, electromagnetic simulation, nanofabrication, MEMS, vacuum systems or experimental microscopy is particularly valuable.
Computational trackExperience or interest in scientific programming, numerical simulation, inverse problems, computational imaging, diffraction or materials characterisation is particularly valuable.

title: PhD in Quantum Physics - Rare-earth Ion Single Photon Emitter at TU Delft, Netherlands
description:
Project Overview

Can silicon play a critical role in building the next generation of the internet - the quantum internet? To realise a fully functional and scalable quantum network, the Groeblacher Lab is developing highly coherent single photon emitters using erbium ions operating in the telecom C-band and directly embedded in a solid-state crystal such as silicon.

The project realises high-quality light-matter interfaces and directly enhances photon emission into an optical channel using photonic crystal cavities. By leveraging different isotopes for long-lived and programmable quantum registers, the team plans to realise all the critical parts of a quantum network using fully integrated and highly scalable structures.

Research Areas

  • Rare-earth ion physics and single emitters in solid-state systems
  • Photonic crystal cavities for enhanced photon emission
  • Experimental AMO and quantum optics techniques
  • Finite-element simulation and advanced computer-based experimentation

title: PhD Student in Limnology: Modelling Phytoplankton Succession in Lakes at Uppsala University, Sweden
description:
Project Overview

The Department of Ecology and Genetics, Limnology programme, at Uppsala University advertises a PhD student position in limnology: modelling phytoplankton succession in lakes (reference UFV-PA 2026/2846). The project explores the driving processes behind phytoplankton succession and assesses how phytoplankton will respond to future environmental changes.

Using process-based biogeochemical models, the doctoral student will study how environmental changes - such as climate warming, eutrophication and extreme weather - affect succession patterns in phytoplankton, and identify conditions that favour specific functional groups. The work improves forecasting of phytoplankton communities with direct applications to lake ecosystem function and drinking-water supply.

Duties and Research Focus

  • Data management and process-based, dynamic modelling of lake ecosystems
  • Simulating phytoplankton succession under climate and nutrient scenarios
  • Teaching, coursework and collaboration within the research group
  • The position sits at the intersection of physics, biogeochemistry and ecology, with a strong numerical component

What RISE Germany Is

RISE Germany (Research Internships in Science and Engineering) is a DAAD programme that pairs undergraduate students from around the world with doctoral researchers at German universities and institutes. The interns work on a real research project for a summer - typically two to three months in 2027 - inside a working lab rather than a classroom. Placements span biology, chemistry, physics, earth sciences, engineering and computer science, and each internship is tied to a specific PhD project that a doctoral student has proposed to host an assistant.

The arrangement works both ways: the PhD student gets a motivated assistant for the summer, and the intern gets a first, honest look at what doctoral research actually involves. For students considering a research career - and especially those planning to apply for master's or PhD positions in Germany later - it is one of the most useful short experiences available.

What You Get

Scholarship components
ComponentDetails
Monthly stipend€992 per month for a full month of the internship, paid by DAAD.
Travel within Germany€160 allowance to cover local and domestic travel.
International travelAn international travel allowance is included in the scholarship package.
PlacementA matched summer research placement with a German doctoral project in summer 2027.

Eligibility and Fit

Who should apply
CriterionRequirement
Study levelEnrolled undergraduate (bachelor's) students in science, engineering or a closely related subject.
StageThe programme is aimed at students who are still completing their first degree; check the official requirements page for the exact year-of-study rules.
LanguageThe working language of RISE placements is English; German is not required.
NationalityOpen to international undergraduate students; there is no single-country restriction.

Application Dates and Process

Key dates for the 2027 round
ComponentDetails
Portal opened15 October 2026
Deadline30 November 2026, 11:59 pm CET
MatchingComplete applications are forwarded to internship providers after DAAD's review; providers may contact shortlisted applicants directly.
Internship periodSummer 2027 (typically 2-3 months, agreed with the host)

How to Apply

Applications are submitted only through the RISE Germany online database portal, which is the link on this page. After registering, candidates upload their documents and can indicate the projects that match their interests; DAAD then reviews complete applications and passes them to the hosting doctoral researchers. There is no application fee, and the entire process - matching, notification and placement - runs through the portal, so it pays to draft your documents well before the 30 November cut-off.

Why This Programme Is Worth Your Time

Germany's doctoral system is employment-based, and supervisors there place real weight on prior lab experience when hiring. A RISE summer gives you that experience with a German research group, a reference who can vouch for your lab work, and a realistic preview of the German academic environment - all while being paid. Students who complete RISE frequently go on to DAAD-funded master's study or doctoral positions in Germany.

  • RISE Germany programme overview (official DAAD)

title: IMPRS-CPQM PhD Positions in Quantum Materials - Max Planck, TU Dresden and St Andrews
description:
Programme Overview

The International Max Planck Research School for Chemistry and Physics of Quantum Materials (IMPRS-CPQM) has opened its 2027 call with more than twenty doctoral projects on offer. The school is a tri-institutional collaboration: the Max Planck Institute for Chemical Physics of Solids in Dresden, Technische Universitaet Dresden, and the University of St Andrews in Scotland. Each project pairs a specific supervisor with a defined research question across condensed matter physics and solid-state chemistry.

The subject matter spans the chemistry-physics boundary of quantum materials - how new compounds are grown and characterised, and how their electronic, magnetic and topological behaviour is measured and modelled. Because every project is advertised individually with its own page, applicants should read the project list on the school website and target the two or three projects closest to their background.

What Is on Offer

The 2027 call at a glance
ComponentDetails
ProjectsMore than 20 doctoral projects in condensed matter physics and solid-state chemistry.
InstitutionsMax Planck Institute for Chemical Physics of Solids (Dresden), TU Dresden, University of St Andrews.
FundingFully funded doctoral employment contracts under Max Planck Society / TU Dresden scales; health insurance, pension and social benefits included.
DeadlineApplications accepted no later than 30 November 2026.
EligibilityHighly motivated candidates with an outstanding bachelor's or master's degree well aligned with the school's research areas.

Who Should Apply

Candidates finishing a bachelor's or master's degree in physics, chemistry, materials science or a neighbouring field whose interests sit in quantum materials - superconductivity, magnetism, topology, correlated electron systems, crystal growth or the solid-state chemistry behind them. The school explicitly welcomes applications from candidates whose degree is 'well-aligned' rather than identical to the project topics, so a strong methods background matters more than an exact subject match.

How to Apply

Applications run through the school's own application system, following the detailed application guidelines published on the IMPRS-CPQM website. The usual package - CV, transcripts, two referees and a statement of research interests tied to specific advertised projects - should be prepared before starting the form, and each project page on the school site tells you which supervisor to reference.

Why Dresden

Dresden is one of Europe's densest clusters for materials research: the Max Planck Institute for Chemical Physics of Solids, TU Dresden's ct.qmat cluster and a wider campus of Leibniz institutes sit within walking distance of each other. Doctoral researchers in Max Planck schools are employed with full contracts, and Dresden's living costs remain well below those of Munich, Stuttgart or Frankfurt, which stretches a German doctoral salary a long way.

Official Sources

  • Official advert and application (verified link)
  • IMPRS-CPQM official website (project list and guidelines)

English language requirements

German doctoral employment generally has no fixed IELTS or TOEFL threshold; your English is judged from the written application and the interview, and prior English-medium study is widely accepted as evidence.

description:
Programme Overview

The Presidential PhD Scholar Programme is the University of Hong Kong's top-tier recruitment scholarship for doctoral students. It sits above HKU's standard postgraduate studentships: every full-time PhD applicant to HKU is automatically considered for it, and the university uses it to attract candidates who would otherwise default to the US, UK or Singapore. There is no separate scholarship form - your PhD application in the Main Round is the application.

What the Scholarship Pays

Benefit stack (2027/28 figures as published by HKU)
ComponentDetails
Postgraduate scholarshipHK$28,700 per month during the normative study period.
Cash awardHK$40,000 in year 1, then HK$20,000 per year for the remaining normative period.
FeesFull waiver of composition fees (HK$49,500 per year) for the whole normative study period.
Conference travelHK$14,400 per year for conference and research-related travel.
First-year totalUp to around HK$445,800 (about US$57,150) in year 1; subsequent years up to around HK$428,300.
HousingGuaranteed hall place in year 1, with the possibility of renewal.
ExtensionFinancial support for an additional year of study for selected outstanding scholars.

Eligibility and Selection

Who gets it
CriterionDetails
AdmissionCandidates applying to the full-time PhD programme at HKU; all Main Round applicants are considered.
ProfileOutstanding academic record, strong research potential and clear fit with the proposed supervisor and department.
ProcessShortlisted candidates may be invited to interview; selection runs alongside PhD admission decisions.

Application Dates

Main Round timeline
StageDetails
Window1 September - 1 December 2026 for the Main Round.
Deadline1 December 2026 (submit early - departments process references on their own schedules).
StartSuccessful candidates typically begin their PhD in September 2027.

How to Apply

Apply through HKU's online research degree application system: identify a supervisor in your field before applying (a confirmed supervisor match matters enormously at HKU), prepare transcripts, CV, research proposal and two academic references, and submit in the Main Round. Because every PhD applicant is considered for the Presidential programme, the practical strategy is to make the research proposal and supervisor conversation as strong as possible rather than treating the scholarship as a separate hurdle.

About HKU

The University of Hong Kong is Hong Kong's oldest university and consistently ranks among Asia's top three research institutions. Its Graduate School administers all research postgraduate admissions and the scholarship schemes attached to them, and doctoral students in most disciplines are supported by university studentships alongside the competitive top-up schemes like HPPS.

Project Overview

TU Delft is recruiting several PhD candidates to join the Taminiau Lab at QuTech for research on quantum networks based on spin defects in silicon carbide (SiC). The project develops SiC devices that enable fast optical entanglement links and high-fidelity spin-qubit control, combining the design and fabrication of nano-photonic SiC devices with quantum optics experiments.

The goal is to demonstrate small but scalable quantum networks for distributed quantum computation, simulations and communication. The Taminiau Lab is an international and collaborative group where people from different backgrounds work closely together, share ideas openly and support each other's development.

Research Areas

  • Spin defects in silicon carbide for quantum networking
  • Design and fabrication of nano-photonic SiC devices

  • High-fidelity spin-qubit control for scalable quantum networks

TU Delft is a technical university in Delft, the Netherlands. The position is hosted in the Taminiau Lab at QuTech, the institute for quantum technology shared by TU Delft and the Netherlands Organisation for Applied Scientific Research (TNO), whose mission is to develop scalable prototypes of a quantum computer and a quantum internet.

title: France Excellence Eiffel Scholarship 2027 (Master's and PhD in France)
description:
Programme Overview

The Eiffel scholarship is the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs' flagship instrument for attracting top international students to French higher education. It exists at two levels - master's and doctoral - and it is deliberately run through institutions: French universities and grandes écoles nominate the candidates they most want to keep. That design detail shapes everything about how you apply, because there is no direct application to Campus France.

At doctoral level the scholarship funds up to 36 months of thesis work in France; at master's level it funds M1-plus-M2 tracks up to 24 months (or 12 months where the institution nominates only the final M2 year). The programme covers four disciplinary clusters: science and technology, economics and management, law and political science, and - at master's level only - a limited set of other fields.

What the Scholarship Pays

Allowances and benefits
ComponentDetails
Master's allowance€1,181 per month, paid on top of direct services such as transport and cultural activities.
Doctoral allowance€1,700 per month.
TravelInternational return journey covered, plus an allowance for the first installation period.
InsuranceHealth insurance cover under the French student scheme and personal liability cover.
Not includedTuition fees are not paid by the Eiffel programme itself - many institutions waive or reduce fees for their Eiffel laureates, but that is decided by the host institution.

Eligibility

Key criteria for the 2027 campaign
CriterionRequirement
NationalityForeign (non-French) nationals; candidates with dual French citizenship are excluded.
Age - master'sUp to 29 years old under the limits published on the official programme page.
Age - PhDUp to 35 years old.
RouteOnly applications submitted by French higher education institutions are accepted; candidates cannot apply to Campus France directly.
Prior attemptsA candidate previously refused at master's level may reapply at doctoral level; laureates cannot receive a second Eiffel at the same level.

Application Timeline

How the campaign runs
StageDetails
Your move firstApply for admission to a French master's or doctoral programme in autumn 2026 and ask the institution to nominate you for Eiffel.
Institution deadlineEach institution sets its internal deadline well before the national cut-off - ask your contact at the university early.
Institution submissionFrench institutions submit nominated files to Campus France by 6 January 2027.
ResultsThe previous campaign published results from late March onwards; expect a similar window for 2027.

How to Approach the Application

Because the institution does the nominating, your real task is to convince a French department that you are worth their nomination slot, not to fill in a scholarship form. That means a strong admission file - grades, a focused study or research plan, and reference letters - plus an early conversation with the programme coordinator about Eiffel nomination. Candidates who contact departments between October and early December have the best chance of being considered, since institutions cap the number of files they forward.

About Campus France

Campus France is the national agency for international mobility and higher education promotion under the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs. It administers the Eiffel programme end-to-end: campaign rules, institutional submissions, selection committee logistics and results publication.

Official Sources

  • Official advert and application (verified link)
  • France Excellence Eiffel programme details (official Campus France)

description:
What These Fellowships Are

The European University Institute in Florence runs a set of named doctoral fellowships that fund the PhD in its four departments. Each carries a scholar's name: the Adam Smith doctoral fellowship in Economics, the Jacob Burckhardt fellowship in History, the Hans Kelsen fellowship in Law, and the Hannah Arendt fellowship in Political and Social Sciences. They are aimed at candidates from a long list of countries across Africa, Asia, the Middle East and Latin America - the official page carries the full nationality table (it includes, among many others, Pakistan, India and Bangladesh).

There is a second, quieter route worth knowing: candidates for History, Law and Political and Social Sciences who are not from the listed countries can still be considered if their academic progress has been impeded by an ongoing war or armed conflict, explained in a statement of up to 700 words.

Funding

Fellowship package
ComponentDetails
Monthly grantEUR 1,650 per month (rate applying from 1 January 2026).
Family allowanceAdditional allowance for fellows with a dependent family.
Travel allowanceIncluded in the package.
InsuranceCover provided under the EUI framework.
DurationSupport runs within the EUI doctoral programme's normative period (four years).

Eligibility

Who can apply
CriterionRequirement
NationalityCitizenship of one of the countries listed in the official table (the list is published on the fellowship page).
DegreeA completed master's or equivalent degree in a discipline relevant to the chosen EUI department.
DepartmentsEconomics, History, Law, and Political and Social Sciences.
Exception routeNon-listed nationals in History, Law and Political and Social Sciences affected by ongoing war or armed conflict may apply with a 700-word statement.

Application Dates

Key dates
ComponentDetails
StatusOpen when checked on 22 October 2026
Deadline15 January 2027, 14:00 CET
LocationEuropean University Institute, Florence, Italy

How to Apply

There is no separate funding application. You apply to the EUI doctoral programme through its normal online form, and inside the form you select the EUI Special Doctoral Fellowship Programme option in the Funding Authorities section, stating your nationality in the Justification field. Applicants using the war-affected route attach their statement there. Because the EUI deadline doubles as the main doctoral admission deadline, your research proposal and references do double duty - write them for the department, not the fellowship.

About the EUI

The European University Institute is a doctoral and postdoctoral institution co-founded by the EU member states and located on the hilltop of Fiesole above Florence. Its four departments teach only graduate research degrees, its cohort is one of the most international in Europe, and EUI alumni fill academic and policy positions across the continent.

title: Türkiye Scholarships (Türkiye Bursları) 2027 - Fully Funded Study in Türkiye
description:
Programme Overview

Türkiye Bursları is the Turkish government's flagship scholarship, run by the Presidency for Turks Abroad and Related Communities (YTB). What makes it unusual among national scholarship programmes is that it bundles admission and funding into one application: successful candidates receive not just money but also university and department placement in Türkiye. Applications are submitted online, free of charge, directly to YTB - no agents, no university portals, no application fee.

The programme runs at associate, bachelor's, master's and doctoral level, and it also carries separate research tracks. For many students from South Asia, Africa and the Middle East it is one of the few scholarships that combines a genuine full-ride package with placement at Turkish state universities without requiring a separate admission process.

What the Scholarship Covers

Benefits package (current published rates)
ComponentDetails
Monthly stipendTL 6,500 undergraduate, TL 9,500 master's, TL 13,000 doctoral - amounts are revised periodically, so confirm the figure for 2027 on the official page.
AccommodationFree accommodation in state dormitories.
TuitionUniversity tuition fees covered - the scholarship pays the university, not you.
Language courseA one-year Turkish language course (Türkçe) before or alongside studies.
Health insurancePublic health insurance for the duration of the scholarship.
FlightOne-off international flight ticket to and from Türkiye.
PlacementUniversity and department placement arranged through the scholarship system.

Eligibility

Key criteria
CriterionRequirement
CitizenshipNon-Turkish citizens (and non dual citizens with Türkiye); there is no country-based quota system.
Academic averageMinimum grade thresholds apply by level - for graduate applications the current threshold is 75%; check the official criteria page for your level.
AgeAge ceilings apply per level under the current rules; confirm the exact figures on the official site before applying.
OtherApplicants must not be Turkish university students at the time of application; graduates may apply.

Application Timeline

Expected 2027 round
StageDetails
WindowApplications typically run from 10 January to 20 February; the 2027 closing date is 20 February 2027.
ShortlistCandidates shortlisted by field and country quotas.
InterviewsOnline or in-person interviews for shortlisted candidates (usually spring).
ResultsFinal results and placements announced in summer, with arrival and language course in the months that follow.

How to Apply

Create an application account on the official Türkiye Bursları website, complete the single online form, and upload transcripts, diplomas or enrolment certificates, an identification document and a photo. You can list university preferences in order, and a short personal statement plus (for some tracks) a research proposal matters for selection. Because the form ranks candidates on academic record plus statement quality, spend your effort on those two documents rather than on extra certificates.

A Note on Realism

Türkiye Bursları is highly competitive - hundreds of thousands of applications arrive each year for a limited number of awards. Apply, but treat it as one track among several: the same profile that fits this programme also suits Hungary's Stipendium Hungaricum, various Chinese government scholarship routes and the DAAD EPOS catalogue, all of which run on similar timelines.

title: Swedish Institute Scholarships for Global Professionals (SISGP) 2027-28
description:
Programme Overview

The Swedish Institute Scholarships for Global Professionals is Sweden's main government-funded master's scholarship. It targets future leaders - people who have already worked a few years and now want a master's degree in Sweden - and it is deliberately tied to leadership and sustainable development rather than pure academic merit. The Swedish Institute pays your university tuition directly, gives you a monthly allowance, and plugs you into an alumni network that keeps working in your favour long after graduation.

One structural point catches many applicants out: the scholarship is a two-step process. You must first apply to an eligible Swedish master's programme through universityadmissions.se (16 October 2026 to 15 January 2027), and only then - after you have your programme applications in - can you apply for the SISGP scholarship itself between 8 and 24 February 2027.

What the Scholarship Covers

Benefits
ComponentDetails
Tuition feesFull tuition paid directly by the Swedish Institute to your Swedish university, every semester.
Living allowanceSEK 12,000 per month throughout the study period.
Travel grantSEK 15,000 one-time payment (SEK 10,000 for scholars from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova and Ukraine; not applicable if you already live in Sweden).
InsuranceThe scholarship does not include insurance - check what coverage your university provides for fee-paying and scholarship students.
NetworkMembership of the SI Network for Global Professionals during studies and the SI Alumni Network afterwards.

Eligible Countries (34)

  • Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Belarus, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Egypt, Ethiopia
  • Georgia, Guatemala, Indonesia, Iraq, Jordan, Kenya, Liberia, Malaysia, Mexico, Moldova
  • Morocco, Nigeria, Peru, Philippines, Rwanda, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania, Thailand, Uganda
  • Ukraine, Uzbekistan, Vietnam, Zambia

Work Experience Requirement

Who qualifies
CriterionRequirement
CitizenshipCitizen of one of the 34 eligible countries listed above.
Work experienceAt least 3,000 hours of work experience before February 2027, accumulated from a maximum of three employers (management or leadership in NGO, government, business or academia counts).
Exempt countriesApplicants from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova and Ukraine must provide proof of work experience but are not held to the 3,000-hour minimum.
AdmissionYou must hold (or be awaiting) admission to an eligible Swedish master's programme applied for by 15 January 2027.

Application Timeline

Two steps, two windows
StageDates
Master's applications16 October 2026 - 15 January 2027 via universityadmissions.se
Scholarship application8 - 24 February 2027 (portal closes at 14:59 CET on 24 February)
SI screening25 February - 31 March 2027
Admission notifications1 April 2027 from University Admissions
Final scholarship decisions1 - 22 April 2027

How to Apply

Apply to your chosen master's programmes first, keep your application numbers handy, then complete the SISGP form in the February window with work-experience documentation, leadership evidence and motivation answers. The evaluation weighs professional experience and leadership potential alongside academics, so a supervisor's reference or employer letter that speaks to concrete impact is worth more here than another certificate.

About the Swedish Institute

The Swedish Institute is a government agency working to create interest in Sweden and build relationships with other countries through scholarship programmes, cultural exchange and public diplomacy. Its scholarship portfolio covers master's study, research fellowships and short professional programmes.

Official Sources

  • SISGP official programme page (deadlines and rules)
